288.s: ada̍bdhebhiḥ savitaḥ pā̱yubhi̱ṣṭvam̐ śi̱vebhi̍ra̱dya pari̍ pāhi no̱ gaya̍m hira̍ṇyajihvaḥ suvi̱tāya̱ navya̍se̱ rakṣā̱ māki̍rno a̱ghaśa̍ṃsa īśata
288.d: अद̍ब्धेभिः सवितः पा̱युभि̱ष्ट्वम्̐ शि̱वेभि̍र̱द्य परि̍ पाहि नो̱ गय̍म् हिर̍ण्यजिह्वः सुवि̱ताय̱ नव्य̍से̱ रक्षा̱ माकि̍र्नो अ̱घश̍ंस ईशत
288.m:
With your unbeguiled, benevolent guardians, O Savitṛ, / protect our household today.
Golden-tongued, protect us for newer prosperity; / let no malicious speaker have power over us.

288.s:
asyājarāsaḥ saptadaśa
āpaścid dvādaśa
vibhrāṭ caturdaśa
prabāhuja ekādaśa
pravāyuṃ pañcadaśa
pradīrayeti ca pañcadaśa
ṣaḍanuvākeṣu caturaśītiḥ
288.d:
अस्याजरासः सप्तदश
आपश्चिद् द्वादश
विभ्राट् चतुर्दश
प्रबाहुज एकादश
प्रवायुं पञ्चदश
प्रदीरयेति च पञ्चदश
षडनुवाकेषु चतुरशीतिः

289.s: yajjāgra̍to dū̱ramudai̍ti̱ daiva̱ṃ tadu̍ su̱ptasya̱ tathai̱vaiti̍ dū̱ra̱ṃga̱maṃ jyorti̍ṣā̱ṃ jyoti̱reka̱ṃ tanme̱ mana̍ḥ śi̱vasa̍ṅkalpamastu
289.d: यज्जाग्र̍तो दू̱रमुदै̍ति̱ दैव̱ं तदु̍ सु̱प्तस्य̱ तथै̱वैति̍ दू̱र̱ंग̱मं ज्योर्ति̍षा̱ं ज्योति̱रेक̱ं तन्मे̱ मन̍ः शि̱वस̍ङ्कल्पमस्तु
289.m:
That divine [mind] which departs far when awake, / and which likewise returns when asleep,
that far-ranging, single light of lights— / may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

289.s: pi̱tuṃ nu sto̍ṣaṃ ma̱ho dha̱rmāṇa̱ṃ tavi̍ṣīm | yasya̍ tri̱to vyoja̍sā vṛ̱traṃ vipa̍rvama̱rdaya̍t
289.d: पि̱तुं नु स्तो̍षं म̱हो ध̱र्माण̱ं तवि̍षीम् । यस्य̍ त्रि̱तो व्योज̍सा वृ̱त्रं विप̍र्वम̱र्दय̍त्
289.m: Now will I praise food, the great supporter, the strength, / through whose power Trita / crushed Vṛtra joint by joint.

289.s: anvi̱da̍numate̱ tvaṃ manyā̍sai̱ śaṃ ca̍ naskṛdhi kratve̱ dakṣā̍ya no hinu̱ pra ṇa̱ āyū̍m̐ṣi tāriṣaḥ
289.d: अन्वि̱द̍नुमते̱ त्वं मन्या̍सै̱ शं च̍ नस्कृधि क्रत्वे̱ दक्षा̍य नो हिनु̱ प्र ण̱ आयू̍म्̐षि तारिषः
289.m:
O Anumati, do you consent to us, / and grant us welfare;
impel us to purpose, to capability; / lengthen our lifespans.

289.s: sinī̍vāli pṛ̱thuṣṭu̍ke̱ yā de̱vānā̱masi̱ svasā̍ | ju̱ṣasva̍ ha̱vyamāhu̍taṃ pra̱jāṃ de̍vi didiḍḍhi naḥ
289.d: सिनी̍वालि पृ̱थुष्टु̍के̱ या दे̱वाना̱मसि̱ स्वसा̍ । जु̱षस्व̍ ह̱व्यमाहु̍तं प्र̱जां दे̍वि दिदिड्ढि नः
289.m:
O Sinīvālī of broad tufts, / you who are the sister of the gods,
enjoy the oblation offered; / bestow offspring upon us, O goddess.

289.s: pañca̍ na̱dyaḥ sara̍svatī̱mapi̍ yanti sasro̍tasaḥ | sara̍svatī tu pa̍ñca̱dhā so de̱śe'bha̍vatsa̱rit
289.d: पञ्च̍ न̱द्यः सर̍स्वती̱मपि̍ यन्ति सस्रो̍तसः । सर̍स्वती तु प̍ञ्च̱धा सो दे̱शेऽभ̍वत्स̱रित्
289.m:
Five rivers flow into the Sarasvatī, / having common streams;
the Sarasvatī then became fivefold / a stream in that land.

289.s: tvama̍gne pratha̱mo aṅgi̍rā ṛṣi̍rde̱vo de̱vānā̍mabhavaḥ śi̱vaḥ sakhā̍ tava̍ vra̱te ka̱vayo̍ vidma̱nāpa̱so'jā̍yanta ma̱ruto̍ bhrāja̍dṛṣṭayaḥ
289.d: त्वम̍ग्ने प्रथ̱मो अङ्गि̍रा ऋषि̍र्दे̱वो दे̱वाना̍मभवः शि̱वः सखा̍ तव̍ व्र̱ते क̱वयो̍ विद्म̱नाप̱सोऽजा̍यन्त म̱रुतो̍ भ्राज̍दृष्टयः
289.m:
You, O Agni, as the first Aṅgiras ṛṣi, / a god, became the auspicious friend of the gods;
in your commandment the poets, working with skill, / were born, the Maruts with shining spears.

289.s: tvaṃ no̍ agne̱ tava̍ deva pā̱yubhi̍rma̱ghono̍ rakṣa ta̱nva̍śca vandya trā̱tā to̱kasya̱ tana̍ye̱ gavā̍ma̱syani̍meṣam̐ rakṣa̍māṇasta̱va vra̱te
289.d: त्वं नो̍ अग्ने̱ तव̍ देव पा̱युभि̍र्म̱घोनो̍ रक्ष त̱न्व̍श्च वन्द्य त्रा̱ता तो̱कस्य̱ तन̍ये̱ गवा̍म̱स्यनि̍मेषम्̐ रक्ष̍माणस्त̱व व्र̱ते
289.m:
Do you, O god Agni, with your guardians, / protect us, the bounteous patrons, and our bodies, O praiseworthy one;
you are the protector of child and descendant, of cattle, / keeping watch without blinking in your commandment.

289.s: u̱ttā̱nāyā̍mava̍ bharā ciki̱tvāntsa̱dyaḥ pravī̍tā̱ vṛṣa̍ṇaṃ jajāna a̱ru̱ṣastū̍po̱ ruśa̍dasya̱ pāja̱ iḷā̍yāspu̱tro va̱yune̍'janiṣṭa
289.d: उ̱त्ता̱नाया̍मव̍ भरा चिकि̱त्वान्त्स̱द्यः प्रवी̍ता̱ वृष̍णं जजान अ̱रु̱षस्तू̍पो̱ रुश̍दस्य̱ पाज̱ इऌआ̍यास्पु̱त्रो व̱युने̍ऽजनिष्ट

289.s: iḷā̍yāstvā pa̱de va̱yaṃ nābhā̍ pṛthi̱vyā adhi̍ jā̱tave̍do nidhrī̍ma̱hyagne̍ ha̱vyāya̱ voḷha̍ve
289.d: इऌआ̍यास्त्वा प̱दे व̱यं नाभा̍ पृथि̱व्या अधि̍ जा̱तवे̍दो निध्री̍म̱ह्यग्ने̍ ह̱व्याय̱ वोऌह̍वे
289.m:
In the footprint of Iḷā we / on the navel of the earth,
O Jātavedas, set you down, / O Agni, to carry the oblation.

289.s: pra ma̍nmahe śavasā̱nāya̍ śū̱ṣamāṅgū̱ṣaṃ girva̍ṇase aṅgira̱svat su̱vṛ̱ktibhi̍ stuva̱ta ṛ̱gmiyāyārcā̱mārkaṃ nare̍ vi̱śrutā̍ya
289.d: प्र म̍न्महे शवसा̱नाय̍ शू̱षमाङ्गू̱षं गिर्व̍णसे अङ्गिर̱स्वत् सु̱वृ̱क्तिभि̍ स्तुव̱त ऋ̱ग्मियायार्चा̱मार्कं नरे̍ वि̱श्रुता̍य
289.m:
We meditate an impulse for the powerful one, / a panegyric for the lover of song, like the Aṅgirases;
with well-formed hymns, we, praising the praise-worthy one, / will sing a chant to the famed hero.

289.s: pra vo̍ ma̱he mahi̱ namo̍ bharadhvamāṅgū̱ṣya̍m̐ śavasā̱nāya̱ sāma̍ yenā̍ na̱ḥ pūrve̍ pi̱tara̍ḥ pada̱jñā arca̍nto aṅgira̍so gā avi̍ndan
289.d: प्र वो̍ म̱हे महि̱ नमो̍ भरध्वमाङ्गू̱ष्य̍म्̐ शवसा̱नाय̱ साम̍ येना̍ न̱ः पूर्वे̍ पि̱तर̍ः पद̱ज्ञा अर्च̍न्तो अङ्गिर̍सो गा अवि̍न्दन्
289.m:
Offer forward great homage to the mighty one, / a song fit for panegyric, a sāman for the powerful one,
by which our ancient fathers, knowing the track, / singing praise, the Aṅgirases found the cows.

289.s: i̱cchanti̍ tvā so̱myāsa̱ḥ sakhā̍yaḥ su̱nvanti̱ soma̱ṃ dadha̍ti̱ prayā̍m̐si titi̍kṣante a̱bhiśa̍stiṃ janā̍nā̱mindra̱ tvadā kaśca̱na hi pra̍ke̱taḥ
289.d: इ̱च्छन्ति̍ त्वा सो̱म्यास̱ः सखा̍यः सु̱न्वन्ति̱ सोम̱ं दध̍ति̱ प्रया̍म्̐सि तिति̍क्षन्ते अ̱भिश̍स्तिं जना̍ना̱मिन्द्र̱ त्वदा कश्च̱न हि प्र̍के̱तः
289.m:
Your soma-desiring friends long for you; / they press soma, they offer refreshing drinks;
they endure the reproach of men; / for from you, O Indra, comes any beacon.

289.s: na te̍ dū̱re pa̍ra̱mā ci̱drajā̍m̐syā tu pra yā̍hi hari̱vo hari̍bhyām sthi̱rāya̱ vṛṣṇe̱ sava̍nā kṛ̱temā yu̱ktā grāvā̍ṇaḥ samidhā̱ne a̱gnau
289.d: न ते̍ दू̱रे प̍र̱मा चि̱द्रजा̍म्̐स्या तु प्र या̍हि हरि̱वो हरि̍भ्याम् स्थि̱राय̱ वृष्णे̱ सव̍ना कृ̱तेमा यु̱क्ता ग्रावा̍णः समिधा̱ने अ̱ग्नौ
289.m:
Not far for you are even the highest realms; / drive forth, O lord of bays, with your two bays.
For the steadfast bull these pressings are prepared; / harnessed are the pressing-stones while Agni is kindled.

289.s: aṣā̍ḷhaṃ yu̱tsu pṛta̍nāsu pa̱priṃm̐ sva̱rṣā̱mapsā̍ṃ vṛja̱nasya̍ go̱pām bhare̍ṣu̱jām̐ su̍kṣi̱tim̐ su̱śrava̍sa̱ṃ jaya̍nta̱ṃ tvāmanu̍ madema soma
289.d: अषा̍ऌहं यु̱त्सु पृत̍नासु प̱प्रिंम्̐ स्व̱र्षा̱मप्सा̍ं वृज̱नस्य̍ गो̱पाम् भरे̍षु̱जाम्̐ सु̍क्षि̱तिम्̐ सु̱श्रव̍स̱ं जय̍न्त̱ं त्वामनु̍ मदेम सोम
289.m:
Unconquered in battles, winning in combats, / gaining the sun, gaining the waters, guardian of the clan,
born in contests, dwelling well, renowned, / victorious, may we exult after you, O Soma.

289.s: somo̍ dhe̱num̐ somo̱ arva̍ntamā̱śum̐ somo̍ vī̱raṃ ka̍rma̱ṇya̍ṃ dadāti sā̱da̱nya̍ṃ vi̱dathya̍ṃm̐ sa̱bheya̍ṃ pitṛ̱śrava̍ṇa̱ṃ yo dadā̍śadasmai
289.d: सोमो̍ धे̱नुम्̐ सोमो̱ अर्व̍न्तमा̱शुम्̐ सोमो̍ वी̱रं क̍र्म̱ण्य̍ं ददाति सा̱द̱न्य̍ं वि̱दथ्य̍ंम्̐ स̱भेय̍ं पितृ̱श्रव̍ण̱ं यो ददा̍शदस्मै
289.m:
Soma gives a milch cow, Soma a swift courser, / Soma a valiant hero skilled in action,
fit for the assembly, fit for the council, fit for society, / bringing fame to his fathers, to him who worships him.

289.s: tvami̱mā oṣa̍dhīḥ soma̱ viśvā̱stvama̱po a̍janaya̱stvaṃ gāḥ tvamā ta̍tantho̱rva̱ntari̍kṣa̱ṃ tvaṃ jyorti̍ṣā̱ vi tamo̍ vavartha
289.d: त्वमि̱मा ओष̍धीः सोम̱ विश्वा̱स्त्वम̱पो अ̍जनय̱स्त्वं गाः त्वमा त̍तन्थो̱र्व̱न्तरि̍क्ष̱ं त्वं ज्योर्ति̍षा̱ वि तमो̍ ववर्थ
289.m:
You generated all these plants, O Soma, / you the waters, you the cows;
you stretched out the wide mid-air; / you uncovered the darkness with light.

289.s: de̱vena̍ no̱ mana̍sā deva soma rā̱yo bhā̱gam̐ sa̍hasāvanna̱bhi yu̍dhya mā tvā̱ ta̍nadīśiṣe vī̱rya̍syo̱bhaye̍bhyaḥ praci̍kitsā ga i̍ṣṭau
289.d: दे̱वेन̍ नो̱ मन̍सा देव सोम रा̱यो भा̱गम्̐ स̍हसावन्न̱भि यु̍ध्य मा त्वा̱ त̍नदीशिषे वी̱र्य̍स्यो̱भये̍भ्यः प्रचि̍कित्सा ग इ̍ष्टौ
289.m:
With a divine mind, O divine Soma, / fight for our share of wealth, O mighty one;
let no one harm you, you rule over valor; / take thought for both [parties] in the quest for cattle.

289.s: a̱ṣṭau vya̍khyatka̱kubha̍ḥ pṛthi̱vyāstrī dhanva̱ yoja̍nā sa̱pta sindhū̍n hira̍ṇyākṣaḥ savi̱tā de̱va āgā̱ddadha̱dratnā̍ dā̱śuṣe̱ vāryā̍ṇi
289.d: अ̱ष्टौ व्य̍ख्यत्क̱कुभ̍ः पृथि̱व्यास्त्री धन्व̱ योज̍ना स̱प्त सिन्धू̍न् हिर̍ण्याक्षः सवि̱ता दे̱व आगा̱द्दध̱द्रत्ना̍ दा̱शुषे̱ वार्या̍णि
289.m:
He has looked out over the eight peaks of the earth, / the three waste-land leagues, the seven rivers.
Golden-eyed, the god Savitṛ has come, / bestowing desirable treasures upon the worshipper.

289.s: hira̍ṇyapāṇiḥ savi̱tā vi̍carṣa̱ṇiru̱bhe dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī a̱ntarī̍yate apāmīvā̍ṃ bādha̍te̱ veti̱ sūrya̍ma̱bhi kṛ̱ṣṇena̱ raja̍sā̱ dyāmṛ̍ṇoti
289.d: हिर̍ण्यपाणिः सवि̱ता वि̍चर्ष̱णिरु̱भे द्यावा̍पृथि̱वी अ̱न्तरी̍यते अपामीवा̍ं बाध̍ते̱ वेति̱ सूर्य̍म̱भि कृ̱ष्णेन̱ रज̍सा̱ द्यामृ̍णोति
289.m:
Golden-handed Savitṛ, active, / moves between both heaven and earth;
he drives away disease, he approaches the sun; / he covers heaven with the dark realm.

289.s: hira̍ṇyahasto asu̍raḥ sunī̱thaḥ su̍mṛḷī̱kaḥ svavā̍ yātva̱rvāṅ a̱pa̱sedha̍nrakṣaso̍ yātudhā̱nānasthā̍dde̱vaḥ pra̍tido̱ṣaṃ gṛ̍ṇā̱naḥ
289.d: हिर̍ण्यहस्तो असु̍रः सुनी̱थः सु̍मृऌई̱कः स्ववा̍ यात्व̱र्वाङ् अ̱प̱सेध̍न्रक्षसो̍ यातुधा̱नानस्था̍द्दे̱वः प्र̍तिदो̱षं गृ̍णा̱नः
289.m:
Golden-handed asura, of good guidance, / most gracious, wealthy, may he come hither;
driving off demons and sorcerers, / the god has taken his stand, praised at nightfall.

289.s: ye te̱ panthā̍ḥ savitaḥ pū̱rvyāso̍'re̱ṇava̍ḥ sukṛ̍tā a̱ntari̍kṣe tebhi̍rno a̱dya pa̱thibhi̍ḥ su̱gebhī̱ rakṣā̍ ca no̱ adhi̍ ca brūhi deva
289.d: ये ते̱ पन्था̍ः सवितः पू̱र्व्यासो̍ऽरे̱णव̍ः सुकृ̍ता अ̱न्तरि̍क्षे तेभि̍र्नो अ̱द्य प̱थिभि̍ः सु̱गेभी̱ रक्षा̍ च नो̱ अधि̍ च ब्रूहि देव
289.m:
The paths of yours, O Savitṛ, that are ancient, / dustless, well-made in the mid-air,
by those paths, easy to travel, protect us today, / and speak for us, O god.

289.s: u̱bhā pi̍batamaśvino̱bhā na̱ḥ śarma̍ yacchatam | a̱vi̱dri̱yābhi̍rū̱tibhi̍ḥ
289.d: उ̱भा पि̍बतमश्विनो̱भा न̱ः शर्म̍ यच्छतम् । अ̱वि̱द्रि̱याभि̍रू̱तिभि̍ः
289.m: Do both drink, O Aśvins, / do both grant us shelter / with unceasing aids.

289.s: a̱pra̱svatīmaśvinā̱ vāca̍ma̱sme kṛ̱taṃ no̍ dasrā vṛṣaṇā manī̱ṣām a̱dyutye̍'va̍se̱ nihva̍ye vāṃ vṛ̱dhe ca̍ no bhavata̱ṃ vāja̍sātau
289.d: अ̱प्र̱स्वतीमश्विना̱ वाच̍म̱स्मे कृ̱तं नो̍ दस्रा वृषणा मनी̱षाम् अ̱द्युत्ये̍ऽव̍से̱ निह्व̍ये वां वृ̱धे च̍ नो भवत̱ं वाज̍सातौ
289.m:
Make our speech full of work, O Aśvins, / make our prayer [fruitful], O wondrous, bull-like ones;
I invoke you both for aid in the unceasing [sacrifice], / and be for our increase in the winning of vital vigor.

289.s: dyu̱bhi̍ra̱ktubhi̱: pari̍ pātama̱smānari̍ṣṭebhiraśvinā̱ saubha̍gebhiḥ tanno̍ mi̱tro varu̍ṇo māmahantā̱madi̍ti̱: sindhu̍: pṛthi̱vī u̱ta dyauḥ
289.d: द्यु̱भि̍र̱क्तुभि̱: परि̍ पातम̱स्मानरि̍ष्टेभिरश्विना̱ सौभ̍गेभिः तन्नो̍ मि̱त्रो वरु̍णो मामहन्ता̱मदि̍ति̱: सिन्धु̍: पृथि̱वी उ̱त द्यौः
289.m: Protect us by day and by night with uninjured fortunes, O Aśvins; / let Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven magnify this for us.

289.s: ā kṛ̱ṣṇena̱ raja̍sā̱ varta̍māno nive̱śaya̍nna̱mṛta̱ṃ martya̍ṃ ca hi̱ra̱ṇyaye̍na savi̱tā rathe̱nā de̱vo yā̍ti̱ bhuva̍nāni̱ paśya̍n
289.d: आ कृ̱ष्णेन̱ रज̍सा̱ वर्त̍मानो निवे̱शय̍न्न̱मृत̱ं मर्त्य̍ं च हि̱र̱ण्यये̍न सवि̱ता रथे̱ना दे̱वो या̍ति̱ भुव̍नानि̱ पश्य̍न्
289.m: Rolling through the dark realm, laying to rest the immortal and the mortal, / god Savitṛ comes on his golden chariot, looking upon all beings.

290.s: (1) ā rā̍tri̱ pārthi̍va̱m̐ raja̍: pi̱tura̍prāyi̱ dhāma̍bhiḥ di̱vaḥ sadā̍m̐si bṛha̱tī vi ti̍ṣṭhasa̱ ā tve̱ṣaṃ va̍rtate̱ tama̍:
290.d: (1) आ रा̍त्रि̱ पार्थि̍व̱म्̐ रज̍: पि̱तुर̍प्रायि̱ धाम̍भिः दि̱वः सदा̍म्̐सि बृह̱ती वि ति̍ष्ठस̱ आ त्वे̱षं व̍र्तते̱ तम̍:
290.m: The earthly realm has been filled with the lights of Father [Heaven], O Night; / you, the lofty one, bestride the seats of heaven; glittering darkness rolls forth.

290.s: u̱ṣastacci̱tramā bha̍rā̱smabhya̍ṃ vājinīvati | yena̍ to̱kaṃ ca̱ tana̍ya̱ṃ ca̱ dhāma̍he
290.d: उ̱षस्तच्चि̱त्रमा भ̍रा̱स्मभ्य̍ं वाजिनीवति । येन̍ तो̱कं च̱ तन̍य̱ं च̱ धाम̍हे
290.m: Bring us that brilliant wealth, O Dawn rich in reward, / by which we may establish both children and lineage.

290.s: prā̱ta̱rjita̱ṃ bhaga̍mu̱gram̐ hu̍vema va̱yaṃ pu̱tramadi̍te̱ryo vi̍dha̱rtā ā̱dhraści̱dyaṃ manya̍mānastu̱raści̱drājā̍ ci̱dyaṃ bhaga̍ṃ bha̱kṣītyāha̍
290.d: प्रा̱त̱र्जित̱ं भग̍मु̱ग्रम्̐ हु̍वेम व̱यं पु̱त्रमदि̍ते̱र्यो वि̍ध̱र्ता आ̱ध्रश्चि̱द्यं मन्य̍मानस्तु̱रश्चि̱द्राजा̍ चि̱द्यं भग̍ं भ̱क्षीत्याह̍
290.m: Let us invoke the fierce Bhaga, victorious in the morning, the son of Aditi who is the supporter, / about whom the poor man, reflecting, and the swift man, and even the king says: "May I share in Bhaga!"

290.s: pū̱ṣantava̍ vra̱te va̱yaṃ na ri̍ṣyema̱ kadā̍ ca̱na | sto̱tāra̍sta ihasmasi
290.d: पू̱षन्तव̍ व्र̱ते व̱यं न रि̍ष्येम̱ कदा̍ च̱न । स्तो̱तार̍स्त इहस्मसि
290.m: O Pūṣan, under your vow may we never suffer harm; / here we are your praisers.

290.s: pa̱thaspa̍tha̱: pari̍patiṃ vaca̱syā kāme̍na kṛ̱to a̱bhyāna̍ḷa̱rkam sa no̍ rāsacchu̱rudha̍śca̱ndrāgrā̱ dhiya̍ṃdhiyam̐ sīṣadhāti̱ pra pū̱ṣā
290.d: प̱थस्प̍थ̱: परि̍पतिं वच̱स्या कामे̍न कृ̱तो अ̱भ्यान̍ऌअ̱र्कम् स नो̍ रासच्छु̱रुध̍श्च̱न्द्राग्रा̱ धिय̍ंधियम्̐ सीषधाति̱ प्र पू̱षा
290.m: With longing desire, the singer with his song has reached the guardian lord of every path; / may he, Pūṣan, grant us invigorating gifts crowned with delight; may he make every insight succeed.

290.s: trīṇi̍ pa̱dā vi ca̍krame̱ viṣṇu̍rgo̱pā adā̍bhyaḥ | ato̱ dharmā̍ṇi dhā̱raya̍n
290.d: त्रीणि̍ प̱दा वि च̍क्रमे̱ विष्णु̍र्गो̱पा अदा̍भ्यः । अतो̱ धर्मा̍णि धा̱रय̍न्
290.m: Viṣṇu, the uncheatable guardian, strode out three steps, / upholding the sacred ordinances from there.

290.s: tadviprā̍so vipa̱nyavo̍ jāgṛ̱vām̐sa̱: sami̍ndhate | viṣṇo̱ryatpa̍ra̱maṃ pa̱dam
290.d: तद्विप्रा̍सो विप̱न्यवो̍ जागृ̱वाम्̐स̱: समि̍न्धते । विष्णो̱र्यत्प̍र̱मं प̱दम्
290.m: The inspired seers, praising eloquently and vigilant, kindle that— / which is Viṣṇu's highest step.

290.s: ghṛ̱tava̍tī̱ bhuva̍nānāmabhiśri̱yorvī pṛ̍thvī ma̍dhudu̱ghe su̱peśa̍sā dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī varu̍ṇasya̱ dharma̍ṇā̱ viṣka̍bhite a̱jare̱ bhūri̍retasā
290.d: घृ̱तव̍ती̱ भुव̍नानामभिश्रि̱योर्वी पृ̍थ्वी म̍धुदु̱घे सु̱पेश̍सा द्यावा̍पृथि̱वी वरु̍णस्य̱ धर्म̍णा̱ विष्क̍भिते अ̱जरे̱ भूरि̍रेतसा
290.m: Rich in ghee, the refuge of all beings, wide, broad, yielding sweetness, beautifully adorned, / Heaven and Earth, propped apart by Varuṇa's ordinance, ageless, rich in seed.

290.s: ye na̍: sa̱patnā̱ apa̱ te bha̍vantvindrā̱gnibhyā̱mava̍ bādhāmahe̱ tān vasa̍ṃvo ru̱drā ā̍di̱tyā u̍pari̱spṛśa̍ṃ mo̱graṃ cettā̍ramadhirā̱jama̍kran
290.d: ये न̍: स̱पत्ना̱ अप̱ ते भ̍वन्त्विन्द्रा̱ग्निभ्या̱मव̍ बाधामहे̱ तान् वस̍ंवो रु̱द्रा आ̍दि̱त्या उ̍परि̱स्पृश̍ं मो̱ग्रं चेत्ता̍रमधिरा̱जम̍क्रन्
290.m: Those who are our rivals, let them be driven away; with Indra and Agni we push them back; / the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas have made me touch the height, a fierce perceiver, an overlord.

290.s: ā nā̍satyā tri̱bhire̍kāda̱śairi̱ha de̱vebhi̍ryā̱taṃ madhu̍peya̱maśvi̍nā prāyu̱stāri̍ṣṭa̱ṃ nī rapā̍m̐si mṛkṣata̱m̐ sedha̍ta̱ṃ dveṣo̱ bhava̍tam̐ sacā̱bhuvā̍
290.d: आ ना̍सत्या त्रि̱भिरे̍काद̱शैरि̱ह दे̱वेभि̍र्या̱तं मधु̍पेय̱मश्वि̍ना प्रायु̱स्तारि̍ष्ट̱ं नी रपा̍म्̐सि मृक्षत̱म्̐ सेध̍त̱ं द्वेषो̱ भव̍तम्̐ सचा̱भुवा̍
290.m: O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, come here to the drinking of mead together with the thrice-eleven gods; / extend our lifespan, wipe away our afflictions, drive off hatred, be our companions.

290.s: e̱ṣa va̱ stomo̍ maruta i̱yaṃ gīrmāndā̱ryasya̍ mā̱nyasya̍ kā̱roḥ eṣā yā̍sīṣṭa ta̱nve̍ va̱yāṃ vi̱dyāmeṣa̍ṃ vṛ̱jana̍ṃ jī̱radā̍num
290.d: ए̱ष व̱ स्तोमो̍ मरुत इ̱यं गीर्मान्दा̱र्यस्य̍ मा̱न्यस्य̍ का̱रोः एषा या̍सीष्ट त̱न्वे̍ व̱यां वि̱द्यामेष̍ं वृ̱जन̍ं जी̱रदा̍नुम्
290.m: This is your praise, O Maruts; this is the song of Māndārya, of the poet Mānya; / may this approach your body as nourishment; may we find refreshing food and an encampment of flowing waters.

290.s: sa̱hasto̍māḥ sa̱hacha̍ndasa ā̱vṛta̍: sa̱hapra̍mā ṛṣa̍yaḥ sa̱pta daivyā̍: pūrve̍ṣā̱ṃ panthā̍manu̱dṛśya̱ dhīrā̍ a̱nvālai̍bhire ra̱thyo na ra̱śmīn
290.d: स̱हस्तो̍माः स̱हछ̍न्दस आ̱वृत̍: स̱हप्र̍मा ऋष̍यः स̱प्त दैव्या̍: पूर्वे̍षा̱ं पन्था̍मनु̱दृश्य̱ धीरा̍ अ̱न्वालै̍भिरे र̱थ्यो न र̱श्मीन्
290.m: With praise-songs, with meters, with rituals, with standard measures, the seven divine seers, / beholding the path of the ancients, have grasped it as charioteers do the reins.

290.s: ā̱yu̱ṣya̍ṃ varca̱sya̍m̐ rā̱yaspoṣa̍maudbhi̱dam i̱dam̐ hira̍ṇya̱ṃ varca̍sva̱jjaitrā̱yāvi̍śatādu̱ mām
290.d: आ̱यु̱ष्य̍ं वर्च̱स्य̍म्̐ रा̱यस्पोष̍मौद्भि̱दम् इ̱दम्̐ हिर̍ण्य̱ं वर्च̍स्व̱ज्जैत्रा̱यावि̍शतादु̱ माम्
290.m: Giving long life, giving splendor, increase of wealth, breaking forth— / let this splendid gold enter me for victory.

290.s: adhyāyaḥ
290.d: अध्यायः

290.s: kāṇva-saṃhitā
290.d: काण्व-संहिता

290.s: na tadrakṣām̐m̐si na piśācāstara̍nti de̱vānāmoja̍: prathama̱jam̐ hyetat yo bibharti̍ dākṣāya̱ṇam̐ hira̍ṇya̱m̐ sa de̱veṣu̍ kṛṇute dī̱rghamāyu̱: sa ma̍nu̱ṣye̍ṣu kṛṇute dī̱rghamāyu̍:
290.d: न तद्रक्षाम्̐म्̐सि न पिशाचास्तर̍न्ति दे̱वानामोज̍: प्रथम̱जम्̐ ह्येतत् यो बिभर्ति̍ दाक्षाय̱णम्̐ हिर̍ण्य̱म्̐ स दे̱वेषु̍ कृणुते दी̱र्घमायु̱: स म̍नु̱ष्ये̍षु कृणुते दी̱र्घमायु̍:
290.m: Neither demons nor piśācas overcome it; for this is the firstborn power of the gods; / whoever wears the gold of Dakṣa's line creates long life among the gods, creates long life among men.

290.s: yadārba̍dhnandākṣāya̱ṇā hira̍ṇyam̐ śa̱tānī̍kāya sumana̱syamā̍nāḥ tanma̱ ā ba̍dhnāmi śa̱taśā̍radā̱yāyu̍ṣmāñjarada̍ṣṭi̱ryathāsa̍m
290.d: यदार्ब̍ध्नन्दाक्षाय̱णा हिर̍ण्यम्̐ श̱तानी̍काय सुमन̱स्यमा̍नाः तन्म̱ आ ब̍ध्नामि श̱तशा̍रदा̱यायु̍ष्माञ्जरद̍ष्टि̱र्यथास̍म्
290.m: The gold which the descendants of Dakṣa, well-disposed, bound on Śatānīka, / that do I bind on me for a hundred autumns, so that I may live long and attain old age.

290.s: u̱ta no'hi̍rbu̱dhnya̍: śṛṇotva̱ja eka̍pātpṛthi̱vī sa̍mu̱draḥ viśve̍ de̱vā ṛ̍tā̱vṛdho̍ huvā̱nā stu̱tā mantrā̍: ka̱viśa̍stā avantu
290.d: उ̱त नोऽहि̍र्बु̱ध्न्य̍: शृणोत्व̱ज एक̍पात्पृथि̱वी स̍मु̱द्रः विश्वे̍ दे̱वा ऋ̍ता̱वृधो̍ हुवा̱ना स्तु̱ता मन्त्रा̍: क̱विश̍स्ता अवन्तु
290.m: And may Ahi Budhnya hear us, and Aja Ekapād, Earth, and Ocean; / may the All-Gods, increasers of truth, invoked, and the praised mantras chanted by the sages favor us.

290.s: i̱mā gira̍ ādi̱tyebhyo̍ ghṛ̱tasnū̍: sa̱nādrāja̍bhyo ju̱hvā̍ juhomi śṛ̱ṇotu̍ mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā bhago̍ nastuvijā̱to varu̍ṇo̱ dakṣo̱ am̐śa̍:
290.d: इ̱मा गिर̍ आदि̱त्येभ्यो̍ घृ̱तस्नू̍: स̱नाद्राज̍भ्यो जु̱ह्वा̍ जुहोमि शृ̱णोतु̍ मि̱त्रो अ̍र्य̱मा भगो̍ नस्तुविजा̱तो वरु̍णो̱ दक्षो̱ अम्̐श̍:
290.m: These ghee-dripping songs I pour with the ladle to the Ādityas, the eternal kings; / may Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga hear us, and mighty-born Varuṇa, Dakṣa, and Aṃśa.

290.s: sa̱pta ṛṣa̍yaḥ prati̍hitāḥ śarī̍re sa̱pta ra̍kṣanti̱ sadamapra̍mādam sa̱ptāpa̍: svapa̍to lo̱kamī̍yu̱statra̍ jāgṛto asvapna̱jau sa̱trasadā̍ ca de̱vau
290.d: स̱प्त ऋष̍यः प्रति̍हिताः शरी̍रे स̱प्त र̍क्षन्ति̱ सदमप्र̍मादम् स̱प्ताप̍: स्वप̍तो लो̱कमी̍यु̱स्तत्र̍ जागृतो अस्वप्न̱जौ स̱त्रसदा̍ च दे̱वौ
290.m: Seven seers are set firmly in the body; seven protect the seat vigilantly; / the seven waters have gone to the world of the sleeper; there awake the two gods who never sleep and sit together at the sacrificial session.

290.s: utti̍ṣṭha brahma̱ṇaspate de̱vayanta̍stvemahe upa̱ pra ya̍ntu ma̱ruta̍: sudā̱nava̱ indra̍ prā̱śūrbha̍vā sacā̍
290.d: उत्ति̍ष्ठ ब्रह्म̱णस्पते दे̱वयन्त̍स्त्वेमहे उप̱ प्र य̍न्तु म̱रुत̍: सुदा̱नव̱ इन्द्र̍ प्रा̱शूर्भ̍वा सचा̍
290.m: Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati! We who serve the gods beseech you; / may the generous Maruts come forward; O Indra, be swift in our company.

290.s: pra nū̱naṃ brahma̍ṇa̱spati̍rma̱ntraṃ va̍datyu̱kthya̍m yasmi̱nnindro̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā de̱vā okā̍m̐m̐si cakri̱re
290.d: प्र नू̱नं ब्रह्म̍ण̱स्पति̍र्म̱न्त्रं व̍दत्यु̱क्थ्य̍म् यस्मि̱न्निन्द्रो̱ वरु̍णो मि̱त्रो अ̍र्य̱मा दे̱वा ओका̍म्̐म्̐सि चक्रि̱रे
290.m: Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati speaks the sacred formula worthy of praise, / in which Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, the gods have made their abodes.

290.s: brahma̍ṇaspate̱ tvama̱sya ya̱ntā sū̱ktasya̍ bodhi̱ tana̍yaṃ ca jinva viśva̍ṃ tadbha̱draṃ yadava̍nti de̱vā bṛ̱hadva̍dema vi̱dathe̍ suvī̱rā̍: ya i̱mā viśvā̍ vi̱śvaka̍rmā̱ yo na̍: pi̱tānna̍pate'nna̍sya no dehi
290.d: ब्रह्म̍णस्पते̱ त्वम̱स्य य̱न्ता सू̱क्तस्य̍ बोधि̱ तन̍यं च जिन्व विश्व̍ं तद्भ̱द्रं यदव̍न्ति दे̱वा बृ̱हद्व̍देम वि̱दथे̍ सुवी̱रा̍: य इ̱मा विश्वा̍ वि̱श्वक̍र्मा̱ यो न̍: पि̱तान्न̍पतेऽन्न̍स्य नो देहि
290.m: O Brahmaṇaspati, be the guide of this hymn and nourish our lineage; / all that is auspicious which the gods protect—may we speak lofty words at the assembly, rich in heroes. / He who has made all these things, Viśvakarman, who is our father; O lord of food, give us food.

290.s:
yajjāgrataḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ
ārājyekaviṃśatiḥ
dvayoranuvākayoḥ ṣaṭcatvāriṃśat
290.d:
यज्जाग्रतः पञ्चविंशतिः
आराज्येकविंशतिः
द्वयोरनुवाकयोः षट्चत्वारिंशत्
290.m: "Yaj jāgrataḥ" has twenty-five [verses]; "Ā rātti" has twenty-one; in the two anuvākas there are forty-six. / Thus ends the thirty-third chapter in the Śukla Yajurveda Kāṇva Saṃhitā.

291.s: de̱vaṃ savitu̍: prasu̍va ya̱jñaṃ prasu̍va ya̱jñapa̍tiṃ bhagā̍ya di̱vyo ga̍ndha̱rvaḥ ke̍ta̱pūḥ keta̍ṃ naḥ punātu vā̱caspata̍rvāca̍ṃ naḥ svadatu
291.d: दे̱वं सवितु̍: प्रसु̍व य̱ज्ञं प्रसु̍व य̱ज्ञप̍तिं भगा̍य दि̱व्यो ग̍न्ध̱र्वः के̍त̱पूः केत̍ं नः पुनातु वा̱चस्पत̍र्वाच̍ं नः स्वदतु
291.m: O divine Savitṛ, impel the sacrifice; impel the lord of sacrifice for good fortune; / may the heavenly Gandharva, the purifier of intentions, purify our intention; may the lord of speech sweeten our speech.

291.s: tatsa̍ṃvi̱turvare̍ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍: praco̱dayā̍t
291.d: तत्स̍ंवि̱तुर्वरे̍ण्य̱ं भर्गो̍ दे̱वस्य̍ धीमहि । धियो̱ यो न̍: प्रचो̱दया̍त्
291.m: Let us meditate on that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ, / who shall inspire our insights.

291.s: viśvā̍ni deva savitarduri̱tāni̱ parā̍ suva | yadbha̱draṃ tanna̱ ā su̍va
291.d: विश्वा̍नि देव सवितर्दुरि̱तानि̱ परा̍ सुव । यद्भ̱द्रं तन्न̱ आ सु̍व
291.m: Drive away, O divine Savitṛ, all misfortunes; / impel toward us whatever is auspicious.

291.s: vi̱bhaktāra̍m̐ havāmahe vaso̍ści̱trasya̱ rādha̍saḥ | sa̱vitāra̍ṃ nṛ̱cakṣa̍sam
291.d: वि̱भक्तार̍म्̐ हवामहे वसो̍श्चि̱त्रस्य̱ राध̍सः । स̱वितार̍ं नृ̱चक्ष̍सम्
291.m: We invoke the distributor of wealth, of wondrous gift, / Savitṛ who watches over men.

291.s: brahma̍ṇe brāhma̱ṇaṃ kṣa̱trāya̍ rāja̱nya̍ṃ ma̱rudbhyo̱ vaiśya̱ṃ tapa̍se śū̱draṃ tama̍se taska̱raṃ nāra̱kāya̍ vī̱raha̱ṇam | pāpmane̍ klī̱bamākra̍yāyā ayogū̱ kāmā̍ya puṃśca̱lūmati̍kruṣṭāya māga̱dham
291.d: ब्रह्म̍णे ब्राह्म̱णं क्ष̱त्राय̍ राज̱न्य̍ं म̱रुद्भ्यो̱ वैश्य̱ं तप̍से शू̱द्रं तम̍से तस्क̱रं नार̱काय̍ वी̱रह̱णम् । पाप्मने̍ क्ली̱बमाक्र̍याया अयोगू̱ कामा̍य पुंश्च̱लूमति̍क्रुष्टाय माग̱धम्
291.m: For Brahman a brāhmaṇa; for princely power a rājanya; for the Maruts a vaiśya; for ascetic heat a śūdra; for darkness a thief; for hell a killer of heroes; / for evil a eunuch; for buying and selling an ayogū; for desire a harlot; for harsh shouting a Māgadha;

291.s: nṛ̱ttāya̍ sū̱taṃ gī̱tāya̍ śailū̱ṣaṃ dharmā̍ya sabhāca̱raṃ nari̍ṣṭhāyai bhīma̱lam | na̱rmāya̍ re̱bham̐ hasā̍ya kā̱rimā̱nandā̍ya strīṣa̱khaṃ pra̱made̍ kumārīpu̱traṃ me̱dhāyai̍ rathakā̱raṃ dhairyā̍ya̱ takṣā̍ṇam
291.d: नृ̱त्ताय̍ सू̱तं गी̱ताय̍ शैलू̱षं धर्मा̍य सभाच̱रं नरि̍ष्ठायै भीम̱लम् । न̱र्माय̍ रे̱भम्̐ हसा̍य का̱रिमा̱नन्दा̍य स्त्रीष̱खं प्र̱मदे̍ कुमारीपु̱त्रं मे̱धायै̍ रथका̱रं धैर्या̍य̱ तक्षा̍णम्
291.m: For dancing a charioteer; for singing a minstrel; for law a court-goer; for the assembly an intimidating man; / for jesting a singer of praise; for laughter an actor; for pleasure a companion of women; for lust the son of an unmarried maiden; for wisdom a chariot-maker; for resolve a carpenter;

291.s: tapa̍se kaulā̱laṃ mā̱yāyai̍ karmā̱ram̐ rū̱pāya̍ maṇikā̱ram̐ śubhe va̱pam̐ śa̍ra̱vyā̍yā iṣukā̱ram̐ he̱tyai dha̍nuṣkā̱ram | karma̍ṇe jyākā̱raṃ di̱ṣṭāya̍ rajjusa̱rjaṃ mṛ̱tyave̍ mṛgayumanta̍kāya śvani̱nam
291.d: तप̍से कौला̱लं मा̱यायै̍ कर्मा̱रम्̐ रू̱पाय̍ मणिका̱रम्̐ शुभे व̱पम्̐ श̍र̱व्या̍या इषुका̱रम्̐ हे̱त्यै ध̍नुष्का̱रम् । कर्म̍णे ज्याका̱रं दि̱ष्टाय̍ रज्जुस̱र्जं मृ̱त्यवे̍ मृगयुमन्त̍काय श्वनि̱नम्
291.m: For ascetic heat a potter; for artifice a blacksmith; for beauty a jeweller; for auspiciousness a sower; for archery an arrow-maker; for the weapon a bow-maker; / for ritual work a bowstring-maker; for fate a rope-maker; for death a hunter; for the end a keeper of hounds;

291.s:
na̱dībhya̍ḥ pauñji̱ṣṭamṛkṣīkā̍bhyo naiṣā̱daṃ pu̍ruṣavyā̱ghrāya̍ durma̱daṃ gandharvāpsa̱robhyo̱ vrātya̍m pra̱yugbhya̱ unma̍ttam̐ sa̱rpade̱vaja̱nebhyo'pra̍tipaduma̱yebhyaḥ kitā̱yā a̍kita̱vaṃ pi̱śā̱cebhyo̍ bidalakā̱rīṃ yā̍tu̱dhāne̍bhyaḥ kaṇṭakīkā̱rīm
(1)
291.d:
न̱दीभ्य̍ः पौञ्जि̱ष्टमृक्षीका̍भ्यो नैषा̱दं पु̍रुषव्या̱घ्राय̍ दुर्म̱दं गन्धर्वाप्स̱रोभ्यो̱ व्रात्य̍म् प्र̱युग्भ्य̱ उन्म̍त्तम्̐ स̱र्पदे̱वज̱नेभ्योऽप्र̍तिपदुम̱येभ्यः किता̱या अ̍कित̱वं पि̱शा̱चेभ्यो̍ बिदलका̱रीं या̍तु̱धाने̍भ्यः कण्टकीका̱रीम्
(1)
291.m: For rivers a fisherman; for reed-beds an outcast hunter; for the human tiger a madman; for the Gandharvas and Apsarases an outcast; / for yoked teams a lunatic; for serpent-god folk one without footing; for the dice a gambler; for non-gambling a non-gambler; for the Piśācas a female basket-maker; for the Yātudhānas a female maker of thorns.

292.s: sa̱ṃdhaye̍ jā̱raṃ ge̱hāyo̍papa̱timātyai̍ pari̍vitta̱ṃ nirṛ̍tyai parivividā̱namarā̍dhyā edidhiṣu̱pati̍ṃ niṣkṛ̱tyai pe̍śaskā̱rīm̐ sa̱ṃjñānā̍ya smarakā̱rīm | pra̱kā̱modyā̍yopasa̱daṃ varṇā̍yānu̱rudha̍ṃ balā̍yopa̱dām
292.d: स̱ंधये̍ जा̱रं गे̱हायो̍पप̱तिमात्यै̍ परि̍वित्त̱ं निरृ̍त्यै परिविविदा̱नमरा̍ध्या एदिधिषु̱पति̍ं निष्कृ̱त्यै पे̍शस्का̱रीम्̐ स̱ंज्ञाना̍य स्मरका̱रीम् । प्र̱का̱मोद्या̍योपस̱दं वर्णा̍यानु̱रुध̍ं बला̍योप̱दाम्
292.m: For junction, an adulterer; for the household, a paramour; for misery, an elder brother unmarried before the younger; for Nirṛti, a younger brother married before the elder; for failure, the husband of a younger sister married before her elder sister; for expiation, an embroiderer; for mutual understanding, a matchmaker; for free love, a concubine; for color, a compliant woman; for strength, a briber.

292.s: u̱tsā̱debhya̍ḥ ku̱bjaṃ pra̱mude̍ vāma̱naṃ dvā̱rbhyaḥ srāmam̐ sva̱pnā̍yāndhama̱dharmā̍ya badhi̱raṃ pa̱vitrā̍ya bhi̱ṣaja̍m | pra̱jñānā̍ya nakṣa̱trada̱rśamāśi̱kṣāyai̍ pra̱śnina̍mupaśi̱kṣāyai̍ abhipra̱śnina̍ṃ ma̱ryādā̍yai praśnavivā̱kam
292.d: उ̱त्सा̱देभ्य̍ः कु̱ब्जं प्र̱मुदे̍ वाम̱नं द्वा̱र्भ्यः स्रामम्̐ स्व̱प्ना̍यान्धम̱धर्मा̍य बधि̱रं प̱वित्रा̍य भि̱षज̍म् । प्र̱ज्ञाना̍य नक्ष̱त्रद̱र्शमाशि̱क्षायै̍ प्र̱श्निन̍मुपशि̱क्षायै̍ अभिप्र̱श्निन̍ं म̱र्यादा̍यै प्रश्नविवा̱कम्
292.m: For the heights, a hunchback; for joy, a dwarf; for the gates, a cripple; for sleep, a blind man; for unrighteousness, a deaf man; for purification, a physician; for discernment, an astrologer; for enquiry, an interrogator; for thorough enquiry, a cross-examiner; for limits, an arbitrator.

292.s: arme̍bhyo hasti̱paṃ ja̱vāyā̍śva̱paṃ pu̱ṣṭyai̍ gopā̱laṃ vī̱ryā̍yāvipā̱laṃ teja̍se'japā̱lamirā̍yai kīnā̱śam kīlālā̍ya surākā̱raṃ bha̱drāya̍ gṛha̱pam̐ śreya̍se vi̱ttadha̱mādhya̍kṣāyānukṣa̱ttāra̍m
292.d: अर्मे̍भ्यो हस्ति̱पं ज̱वाया̍श्व̱पं पु̱ष्ट्यै̍ गोपा̱लं वी̱र्या̍याविपा̱लं तेज̍सेऽजपा̱लमिरा̍यै कीना̱शम् कीलाला̍य सुराका̱रं भ̱द्राय̍ गृह̱पम्̐ श्रेय̍से वि̱त्तध̱माध्य̍क्षायानुक्ष̱त्तार̍म्
292.m: For ruins, an elephant-keeper; for speed, a horse-keeper; for nourishment, a cowherd; for vigor, a shepherd; for fiery energy, a goatherd; for refreshing drink, a plowman; for sweet drink, a maker of surā; for good fortune, a householder; for better fortune, a dispenser of wealth; for overseeing, an under-servant.

292.s: bhāyai̍ dārvāhā̱raṃ pra̱bhāyā̍ agnye̱dhaṃ bra̱dhnasya̍ vi̱ṣṭapā̍yābhiṣe̱ktāra̱ṃ varṣi̍ṣṭhāya̱ nākā̍ya parive̱ṣṭāra̍m de̱va̱lo̱kāya̍ peśi̱tāra̍ṃ manu̱ṣyalo̱kāya̍ praka̱ritā̱ram̐ sarve̍bhyo lo̱kebhya̍ upase̱ktāra̱mava̍ ṛ̱tyai va̱dhāyo̍pamanthi̱tāra̍ṃ me̱dhāya̍ vāsaḥpalpū̱līṃ pra̍kā̱māya̍ raja̱yitrīm
292.d: भायै̍ दार्वाहा̱रं प्र̱भाया̍ अग्न्ये̱धं ब्र̱ध्नस्य̍ वि̱ष्टपा̍याभिषे̱क्तार̱ं वर्षि̍ष्ठाय̱ नाका̍य परिवे̱ष्टार̍म् दे̱व̱लो̱काय̍ पेशि̱तार̍ं मनु̱ष्यलो̱काय̍ प्रक̱रिता̱रम्̐ सर्वे̍भ्यो लो̱केभ्य̍ उपसे̱क्तार̱मव̍ ऋ̱त्यै व̱धायो̍पमन्थि̱तार̍ं मे̱धाय̍ वासःपल्पू̱लीं प्र̍का̱माय̍ रज̱यित्रीम्
292.m: For brightness, a gatherer of wood; for brilliance, a fire-kindler; for the summit of the sun, an anointer; for the highest firmament, an attendant; for the world of the gods, a carver; for the world of mortals, a scatterer; for all worlds, a sprinker; for decline, a slayer; for pounder, a churner; for intelligence, a washerwoman; for passion, a dyer.

292.s: ṛ̱taye̍ stenahṛ̍da̱yaṃ vai̍raha̱tyāya̍ piśu̱naṃ vivi̍ktyai kṣattā̱ramau̍padra̱ṣṭrayā̍yānukṣa̱ttāra̍ṃ balā̍yānuca̱raṃ bhūmne pa̍riṣka̱ndam | pri̱yāya̍ priyavā̱dina̱mari̍ṣṭyā aśvasā̱dam̐ svargā̍ya lo̱kāya̍ bhāgadu̱ghaṃ varṣi̍ṣṭhāya̱ nākā̍ya parive̱ṣṭāra̍m
292.d: ऋ̱तये̍ स्तेनहृ̍द̱यं वै̍रह̱त्याय̍ पिशु̱नं विवि̍क्त्यै क्षत्ता̱रमौ̍पद्र̱ष्ट्रया̍यानुक्ष̱त्तार̍ं बला̍यानुच̱रं भूम्ने प̍रिष्क̱न्दम् । प्रि̱याय̍ प्रियवा̱दिन̱मरि̍ष्ट्या अश्वसा̱दम्̐ स्वर्गा̍य लो̱काय̍ भागदु̱घं वर्षि̍ष्ठाय̱ नाका̍य परिवे̱ष्टार̍म्
292.m: For movement, a thief at heart; for blood-feud, an informer; for discrimination, a distributor; for oversight, a sub-distributor; for strength, an attendant; for abundance, a runner; for the dear, a speaker of pleasant words; for safety, a horseman; for the heavenly world, a collector of taxes; for the highest firmament, an attendant.

293.s: ma̱nyave̍'yastā̱paṃ krodhā̍ya nisa̱raṃ yogā̍ya yo̱ktāra̱m̐ śokā̍yābhisa̱rtāra̱ṃ kṣemā̍ya vimo̱ktāra̍ṃmutkūlanikū̱lebhya̍stri̱ṣṭina̍m | vapu̍ṣe mānaskṛ̱tam̐ śīlā̍yāñjanīkā̱rīṃ nirṛ̍tyai kośakā̱rīṃ ya̱māyā̱sūm
293.d: म̱न्यवे̍ऽयस्ता̱पं क्रोधा̍य निस̱रं योगा̍य यो̱क्तार̱म्̐ शोका̍याभिस̱र्तार̱ं क्षेमा̍य विमो̱क्तार̍ंमुत्कूलनिकू̱लेभ्य̍स्त्रि̱ष्टिन̍म् । वपु̍षे मानस्कृ̱तम्̐ शीला̍याञ्जनीका̱रीं निरृ̍त्यै कोशका̱रीं य̱माया̱सूम्
293.m: For anger, a smelter of iron; for wrath, an apostate; for yoking, a yoker; for grief, an assailant; for ease, an unyoker; for the ups and downs, one who stands on three legs; for form, a sculptor; for good conduct, a maker of eye-salve; for Nirṛti, a scabbard-maker; for Yama, a barren woman.

293.s: ya̱māya̍ ya̱masū̍matha̱rva̍bhyo'va̍tokām̐ saṃvatsa̱rāya̍ paryā̱yiṇī̍ṃ parivatsa̱rāyāvi̍jātāmidāvatsa̱rāyātī̍tvarīmidvatsa̱rāyā̍ti̱ṣkadva̍rīm | va̱tsa̱rāya̍ vija̱rjarām̐ saṃvatsa̱rāya̍ pali̱knīmṛ̱bhubhyo̍'jinasandham̐ sā̱dhyebhya̍ścarma̱mnam
293.d: य̱माय̍ य̱मसू̍मथ̱र्व̍भ्योऽव̍तोकाम्̐ संवत्स̱राय̍ पर्या̱यिणी̍ं परिवत्स̱रायावि̍जातामिदावत्स̱रायाती̍त्वरीमिद्वत्स̱राया̍ति̱ष्कद्व̍रीम् । व̱त्स̱राय̍ विज̱र्जराम्̐ संवत्स̱राय̍ पलि̱क्नीमृ̱भुभ्यो̍ऽजिनसन्धम्̐ सा̱ध्येभ्य̍श्चर्म̱म्नम्
293.m: For Yama, a mother of twins; for the Atharvans, a woman who miscarries; for the Saṃvatsara, a woman in regular course; for the Parivatsara, a woman who has not borne; for the Idāvatsara, an over-prolific woman; for the Idvatsara, a woman who miscarries through skipping; for the Vatsara, a decrepit woman; for the Saṃvatsara, a gray-haired woman; for the Ṛbhus, a furrier; for the Sādhyas, a tanner.

293.s: saro̍bhyo dhaivaramu̍pasthāva̍rābhyo dā̱śaṃ vai̍śa̱ntābhyo̍ bai̱ndaṃ na̍ḍva̱lābhya̍ḥ śauṣka̍lam pā̱rāya̍ mārgā̱rama̍vā̱rāya̍ kaiva̱rtaṃ tī̱rthebhya̍ ā̱ndaṃ viṣa̍mebhyo mainā̱lam svane̍bhyaḥ pa̱rṇaka̱ṃ guhā̍bhyaḥ kirā̱tam̐ sānu̍bhyo jambha̍ka̱ṃ parva̍tebhyaḥ kiṃpūru̱ṣam
293.d: सरो̍भ्यो धैवरमु̍पस्थाव̍राभ्यो दा̱शं वै̍श̱न्ताभ्यो̍ बै̱न्दं न̍ड्व̱लाभ्य̍ः शौष्क̍लम् पा̱राय̍ मार्गा̱रम̍वा̱राय̍ कैव̱र्तं ती̱र्थेभ्य̍ आ̱न्दं विष̍मेभ्यो मैना̱लम् स्वने̍भ्यः प̱र्णक̱ं गुहा̍भ्यः किरा̱तम्̐ सानु̍भ्यो जम्भ̍क̱ं पर्व̍तेभ्यः किंपूरु̱षम्
293.m: For lakes, a fisherman; for quiet waters, a boatman; for reservoirs, a Bainda; for reed-beds, a dried-fish monger; for the far shore, a hunter; for the near shore, a ferryman; for ford-crossings, an Ānda; for rugged places, a Maināla; for murmuring sounds, a Parṇaka; for caves, a Kirāta; for peaks, a Jambhaka; for mountains, a Kimpuruṣa.

293.s: bī̱bhatsā̱yai pau̍lka̱saṃ varṇā̍ya hiraṇyakā̱raṃ tu̱lāyai̍ vāṇi̱jaṃ pa̍ścāddo̱ṣāya̍ glā̱vina̱ṃ viśve̍bhyo bhū̱tebhya̍ḥ sidhma̱lam | bhūtyai̍ jāga̱raṇa̍mabhū̍tyai svapa̱namātyai̍ janavā̱dina̱ṃ vyṛ̍ddhyā apaga̱lbham̐ sam̐śa̱rāya̍ pracchi̱dam
293.d: बी̱भत्सा̱यै पौ̍ल्क̱सं वर्णा̍य हिरण्यका̱रं तु̱लायै̍ वाणि̱जं प̍श्चाद्दो̱षाय̍ ग्ला̱विन̱ं विश्वे̍भ्यो भू̱तेभ्य̍ः सिध्म̱लम् । भूत्यै̍ जाग̱रण̍मभू̍त्यै स्वप̱नमात्यै̍ जनवा̱दिन̱ं व्यृ̍द्ध्या अपग̱ल्भम्̐ सम्̐श̱राय̍ प्रच्छि̱दम्
293.m: For disgust, a Paulkasa; for color, a goldsmith; for the balance, a merchant; for late fault, a gamester; for all beings, a leper; for prosperity, an alert watcher; for adversity, a sleeper; for distress, a slanderer; for failure, a brazen man; for ruin, a cleaver.

293.s: a̱kṣarā̱jāya̍ kita̱vaṃ kṛ̱tāyā̍dinavada̱rśaṃ tretā̍yai ka̱lpina̍ṃ dvāpa̱rāyā̍dhika̱lpina̍māska̱ndāya̍ sabhāsthā̱ṇuṃ mṛ̱tyave̍ govya̱cchamanta̍kāya goghā̱tam | kṣudhe yo gāṃ vi̍kṛ̱ntanta̱ṃ bhikṣa̍māṇa upa̱tiṣṭha̍ti duṣkṛ̱tāya̍ cara̍kācā̱ryaṃ pāpmane̍ sailaga̱m
293.d: अ̱क्षरा̱जाय̍ कित̱वं कृ̱ताया̍दिनवद̱र्शं त्रेता̍यै क̱ल्पिन̍ं द्वाप̱राया̍धिक̱ल्पिन̍मास्क̱न्दाय̍ सभास्था̱णुं मृ̱त्यवे̍ गोव्य̱च्छमन्त̍काय गोघा̱तम् । क्षुधे यो गां वि̍कृ̱न्तन्त̱ं भिक्ष̍माण उप̱तिष्ठ̍ति दुष्कृ̱ताय̍ चर̍काचा̱र्यं पाप्मने̍ सैलग̱म्
293.m: For the king of dice, a gambler; for the Kṛta cast, an observer of errors; for the Tretā cast, a calculator; for the Dvāpara cast, a super-calculator; for assault, a pillar of the assembly; for Death, a slaughterer of cattle; for the End, a butcher of cattle; for hunger, one who begs as he stands by a cow being cut up; for misdeed, a traveling teacher; for evil, a wanderer in the wild.

294.s: (3) pratiśrutkā̍yā arta̱naṃ ghoṣā̍ya bhaṣamantā̍ya bahuvā̱dina̍mana̱ntāya̍ mū̱kam̐ śabdā̍yāḍambarāghā̱tam | maha̍se vīṇāvā̱daṃ krośā̍ya tūṇava̱dhmama̍varaspa̱rāya̍ śaṅkha̱dhmaṃ vanā̍ya vana̱pama̱nyato̍'raṇyāya dāva̱pam
294.d: (3) प्रतिश्रुत्का̍या अर्त̱नं घोषा̍य भषमन्ता̍य बहुवा̱दिन̍मन̱न्ताय̍ मू̱कम्̐ शब्दा̍याडम्बराघा̱तम् । मह̍से वीणावा̱दं क्रोशा̍य तूणव̱ध्मम̍वरस्प̱राय̍ शङ्ख̱ध्मं वना̍य वन̱पम̱न्यतो̍ऽरण्याय दाव̱पम्
294.m: For the echo, an echoer; for sound, a yelper; for the end, a babbler; for the endless, a mute; for noise, a drum-beater; for majesty, a lute-player; for clamor, a flute-blower; for low pitch, a conch-blower; for the wood, a forest-guard; for the other forest, a fire-watcher.

294.s: na̱rmāya̍ pum̐śca̱lūm̐ hasā̍ya kā̱riṃ yāda̍se śāba̱lyāṃ grā̍ma̱ṇya̍ṃ gaṇakamabhikroṃśa̱kaṃ tānmaha̍se vī̱ṇāvā̱daṃ pā̍ṇi̱ghaṃ tū̍ṇava̱dhmaṃ tābhṛttāyā̍na̱ndāya̍ tala̱vam
294.d: न̱र्माय̍ पुम्̐श्च̱लूम्̐ हसा̍य का̱रिं याद̍से शाब̱ल्यां ग्रा̍म̱ण्य̍ं गणकमभिक्रोंश̱कं तान्मह̍से वी̱णावा̱दं पा̍णि̱घं तू̍णव̱ध्मं ताभृत्ताया̍न̱न्दाय̍ तल̱वम्
294.m: For jest, a courtesan; for laughter, an actor; for monster-creatures, a motley woman; for the village leader, an accountant; for the slanderer, these for majesty; a lute-player, a hand-clapper, a flute-blower, these for dance; for delight, a tambourine-player.

294.s: a̱gnaye̍ pīvā̍naṃ pṛthi̱vyai pī̍ṭhasa̱rpiṇa̍ṃ vā̱yave̍ cāṇḍā̱lama̱ntari̍kṣāya vam̐śana̱rtina̍ṃ di̱ve kha̍la̱tim̐ sūryā̍ya harya̱kṣam | nakṣa̍trebhyaḥ kirmi̱raṃ ca̱ndrama̍se kilā̱samahne̍ śu̱klaṃ pi̍ṅgā̱kṣam̐ rātryai̍ kṛ̱ṣṇaṃ pi̍ṅgā̱kṣam
294.d: अ̱ग्नये̍ पीवा̍नं पृथि̱व्यै पी̍ठस̱र्पिण̍ं वा̱यवे̍ चाण्डा̱लम̱न्तरि̍क्षाय वम्̐शन̱र्तिन̍ं दि̱वे ख̍ल̱तिम्̐ सूर्या̍य हर्य̱क्षम् । नक्ष̍त्रेभ्यः किर्मि̱रं च̱न्द्रम̍से किला̱समह्ने̍ शु̱क्लं पि̍ङ्गा̱क्षम्̐ रात्र्यै̍ कृ̱ष्णं पि̍ङ्गा̱क्षम्
294.m: For Agni, a fat man; for the earth, a cripple who crawls; for Vāyu, a Cāṇḍāla; for mid-air, a pole-dancer; for heaven, a bald man; for the sun, a yellow-eyed man; for the constellations, a spotted man; for the moon, an albino; for the day, a white man with reddish eyes; for the night, a black man with reddish eyes.

294.s: athai̱tānṣṭau virū̍pānā la̍bhate'ti̍śu̱klaṃ cāti̍kṛ̱ṣṇaṃ cāti̍dī̱rghaṃ cāti̍hra̱svaṃ ca ati̍sthū̱laṃ cāti̍kṛ̱śaṃ cāti̍kū̱lvaṃ cāti̍loma̱śaṃ cāśū̍drā abrā̍hma̱ṇāste prā̍jāpa̱tyāḥ mā̱ga̱dhaḥ pu̍ṃśca̱lī klī̱baḥ ki̍ṃta̱vo'śū̍drā abrā̍hma̱ṇāste prā̍jāpa̱tyāḥ
294.d: अथै̱तान्ष्टौ विरू̍पाना ल̍भतेऽति̍शु̱क्लं चाति̍कृ̱ष्णं चाति̍दी̱र्घं चाति̍ह्र̱स्वं च अति̍स्थू̱लं चाति̍कृ̱शं चाति̍कू̱ल्वं चाति̍लोम̱शं चाशू̍द्रा अब्रा̍ह्म̱णास्ते प्रा̍जाप̱त्याः मा̱ग̱धः पु̍ंश्च̱ली क्ली̱बः कि̍ंत̱वोऽशू̍द्रा अब्रा̍ह्म̱णास्ते प्रा̍जाप̱त्याः
294.m: Then he seizes these eight of defective form: one too white, one too black, one too tall, one too short, one too stout, one too thin, one too bald, and one too hairy; not Śūdras, not Brāhmaṇas, they belong to Prajāpati. A Māgadha, a courtesan, a eunuch, a gambler; not Śūdras, not Brāhmaṇas, they belong to Prajāpati.
Deva Savitar: eight. Saṃdhaye jāram: five. Manyave: five. Pratiśrutkāyai: four. In four anuvākas, twenty-two. Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya in the Śukla Yajurveda Kāṇva Saṃhitā.

294.s:
saṃghaye jāraṃ pañca
manyave pañca
pratiśrutkāyai catasraḥ
294.d:
संघये जारं पञ्च
मन्यवे पञ्च
प्रतिश्रुत्कायै चतस्रः

296.s: sa̱hasra̍śīrṣā̱ puru̍ṣaḥ sahasrā̱kṣaḥ sa̱hasra̍pāt sa bhūmi̍ṃm̐ sa̱rvata̍ spṛ̱tvātya̍tiṣṭhaddaśāṅgu̱lam
296.d: स̱हस्र̍शीर्षा̱ पुरु̍षः सहस्रा̱क्षः स̱हस्र̍पात् स भूमि̍ंम्̐ स̱र्वत̍ स्पृ̱त्वात्य̍तिष्ठद्दशाङ्गु̱लम्
296.m: Thousand-headed is the Person, thousand-eyed, thousand-footed. / Having covered the earth on all sides, he stood beyond it by ten finger-breadths.

296.s: puru̍ṣa e̱vedam̐ sarva̱ṃ yadbhūtaṃ yacca̍ bhā̱vya̍m u̱tāmṛ̍ta̱tvasyeśā̍no̱ yadanne̍nāti̱roha̍ti
296.d: पुरु̍ष ए̱वेदम्̐ सर्व̱ं यद्भूतं यच्च̍ भा̱व्य̍म् उ̱तामृ̍त̱त्वस्येशा̍नो̱ यदन्ने̍नाति̱रोह̍ति
296.m: The Person alone is all this, that which has been and that which is to be, / and he is the lord of immortality, which grows beyond through food.

296.s: e̱tāvā̍nasya mahi̱māto jyāyā̍m̐m̐śca̱ pūru̍ṣaḥ pādo̍'sya̱ viśvā̍ bhū̱tāni̍ tri̱pāda̍syā̱mṛta̍ṃ di̱vi
296.d: ए̱तावा̍नस्य महि̱मातो ज्याया̍म्̐म्̐श्च̱ पूरु̍षः पादो̍ऽस्य̱ विश्वा̍ भू̱तानि̍ त्रि̱पाद̍स्या̱मृत̍ं दि̱वि
296.m: Such is his greatness, and greater than that is the Person: / a quarter of him is all beings, three quarters of him is the immortal in heaven.

296.s: tri̱pādū̱rdhva udai̱tpuru̍ṣa̱ḥ pādo̍'sye̱hābha̍va̱tpuna̍ḥ tato̱ viṣva̱ṅ vya̍krāmatsāśanānaśa̱ne a̱bhi
296.d: त्रि̱पादू̱र्ध्व उदै̱त्पुरु̍ष̱ः पादो̍ऽस्ये̱हाभ̍व̱त्पुन̍ः ततो̱ विष्व̱ङ् व्य̍क्रामत्साशनानश̱ने अ̱भि
296.m: With three quarters the Person rose upward; one quarter of him arose here again. / Thence he strode out in all directions toward what eats and what does not eat.

296.s: tato̍ vi̱rāḍa̍jāyata vi̱rājo̱ adhi̱ pūru̍ṣaḥ sa jā̱to atya̍ricyata pa̱ścādbhūmi̱matho̍ pu̱raḥ
296.d: ततो̍ वि̱राड̍जायत वि̱राजो̱ अधि̱ पूरु̍षः स जा̱तो अत्य̍रिच्यत प̱श्चाद्भूमि̱मथो̍ पु̱रः
296.m: From him Virāj was born, and from Virāj the Person. / When born, he extended beyond the earth, behind as well as before.

296.s: tasmā̍dya̱jñātsa̍rva̱huta̱ḥ saṃbhṛ̍taṃ pṛṣadā̱jyam pa̱śūm̐stām̐śca̍kre vāya̱vyā̍nāra̱ṇyā grā̱myāśca̱ ye
296.d: तस्मा̍द्य̱ज्ञात्स̍र्व̱हुत̱ः संभृ̍तं पृषदा̱ज्यम् प̱शूम्̐स्ताम्̐श्च̍क्रे वाय̱व्या̍नार̱ण्या ग्रा̱म्याश्च̱ ये
296.m: From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the dripping ghee was gathered. / He made those beasts of the air, of the forest, and of the village.

296.s: tasmā̍dya̱jñātsa̍rva̱huta̱ ṛca̱ḥ sāmā̍ni jajñire chandā̍ṃm̐si jajñire̱ tasmā̱dyaju̱stasmā̍dajāyata
296.d: तस्मा̍द्य̱ज्ञात्स̍र्व̱हुत̱ ऋच̱ः सामा̍नि जज्ञिरे छन्दा̍ंम्̐सि जज्ञिरे̱ तस्मा̱द्यजु̱स्तस्मा̍दजायत
296.m: From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the verses and the chants were born; / the metres were born from it; the sacrificial formula was born from it.

296.s: tasmā̱daśvā̍ ajāyanta̱ ye ke co̍bha̱yāda̍taḥ gāvo̍ ha jajñire̱ tasmā̱ttasmā̍jjā̱tā a̍jā̱vaya̍ḥ
296.d: तस्मा̱दश्वा̍ अजायन्त̱ ये के चो̍भ̱याद̍तः गावो̍ ह जज्ञिरे̱ तस्मा̱त्तस्मा̍ज्जा̱ता अ̍जा̱वय̍ः
296.m: From it horses were born, and whatever [animals] have teeth in both jaws; / cattle indeed were born from it; from it were born goats and sheep.

296.s: taṃ ya̱jñaṃ ba̱rhiṣi̱ praukṣa̱npuru̍ṣaṃ jā̱tama̍gra̱taḥ tena̍ de̱vā a̍yajanta sā̱dhyā ṛṣa̍yaśca̱ ye
296.d: तं य̱ज्ञं ब̱र्हिषि̱ प्रौक्ष̱न्पुरु̍षं जा̱तम̍ग्र̱तः तेन̍ दे̱वा अ̍यजन्त सा̱ध्या ऋष̍यश्च̱ ये
296.m: They sprinkled as a sacrifice on the sacrificial grass the Person born in the beginning. / With him the gods sacrificed, and the Sādhyas and the ṛṣis.

296.s: yatpuru̍ṣa̱ṃ vyada̍dhuḥ ka̱ti̱dhā vya̍kalpayan mukha̱ṃ kima̍syāsī̱tkiṃ bā̱hū kimūrū pādā̍ ucyete
296.d: यत्पुरु̍ष̱ं व्यद̍धुः क̱ति̱धा व्य̍कल्पयन् मुख̱ं किम̍स्यासी̱त्किं बा̱हू किमूरू पादा̍ उच्येते
296.m: When they partitioned the Person, into how many parts did they arrange him? / What was his mouth? What his two arms? What are his thighs and feet called?

296.s: brā̱hma̱ṇo̍'sya̱ mukha̍māsīdbā̱hū rā̍ja̱nya̍ḥ kṛ̱taḥ ū̱rū tada̍sya̱ yadvaiśya̍ḥ pa̱dbhyām̐ śū̱dro a̍jāyata
296.d: ब्रा̱ह्म̱णो̍ऽस्य̱ मुख̍मासीद्बा̱हू रा̍ज̱न्य̍ः कृ̱तः ऊ̱रू तद̍स्य̱ यद्वैश्य̍ः प̱द्भ्याम्̐ शू̱द्रो अ̍जायत
296.m: The brāhmaṇa was his mouth; his two arms were made the rājanya. / His two thighs, that was the vaiśya; from his feet the śūdra was born.

296.s: ca̱ndramā̱ mana̍so jā̱taścakṣo̱ḥ sūryo̍ ajāyata śrotrā̍dvā̱yuśca̍ prā̱ṇaśca̱ mukhā̍da̱gnira̍jāyata
296.d: च̱न्द्रमा̱ मन̍सो जा̱तश्चक्षो̱ः सूर्यो̍ अजायत श्रोत्रा̍द्वा̱युश्च̍ प्रा̱णश्च̱ मुखा̍द̱ग्निर̍जायत
296.m: The moon was born from his mind; from his eye the sun was born. / From his ear both Vāyu and in-breath; from his mouth Agni was born.

296.s: nābhyā̍ āsīda̱ntari̍kṣam̐ śī̱rṣṇo dyauḥ sama̍vartata pa̱dbhyāṃ bhūmi̱rdiśa̱ḥ śrotrā̱ttathā̍ lo̱kām̐2 a̍kalpayan
296.d: नाभ्या̍ आसीद̱न्तरि̍क्षम्̐ शी̱र्ष्णो द्यौः सम̍वर्तत प̱द्भ्यां भूमि̱र्दिश̱ः श्रोत्रा̱त्तथा̍ लो̱काम्̐2 अ̍कल्पयन्
296.m: From his navel came the mid-air; from his head heaven evolved. / From his two feet the earth, the directions from his ear: thus they arranged the worlds.

296.s: yatpuru̍ṣeṇa ha̱viṣā̍ de̱vā ya̱jñamata̍nvata va̱sa̱nto̍'syāsī̱dājya̍ṃ grī̱ṣma i̱dhmaḥ śa̱raddha̱viḥ
296.d: यत्पुरु̍षेण ह̱विषा̍ दे̱वा य̱ज्ञमत̍न्वत व̱स̱न्तो̍ऽस्यासी̱दाज्य̍ं ग्री̱ष्म इ̱ध्मः श̱रद्ध̱विः
296.m: When the gods stretched the sacrifice with the Person as oblation, / spring was its melted butter, summer the kindling, autumn the oblation.

296.s: sa̱ptāsyā̍sanpari̱dhaya̱striḥ sa̱pta sa̱midha̍: kṛ̱tāḥ de̱vā yadya̱jñaṃ ta̍nvā̱nā aba̍dhna̱npuru̍ṣaṃ pa̱śum
296.d: स̱प्तास्या̍सन्परि̱धय̱स्त्रिः स̱प्त स̱मिध̍: कृ̱ताः दे̱वा यद्य̱ज्ञं त̍न्वा̱ना अब̍ध्न̱न्पुरु̍षं प̱शुम्
296.m: Seven were its enclosing sticks; thrice seven kindling-sticks were made, / when the gods, stretching the sacrifice, bound the Person as the victim.

296.s: ya̱jñena̍ ya̱jñama̍yajanta de̱vāstāni̱ dharmā̍ṇi pratha̱mānyā̍san te ha̱ nāka̍ṃ mahi̱māna̍: sacanta̱ yatra̱ pūrve̍ sā̱dhyāḥ santi̍ de̱vāḥ
296.d: य̱ज्ञेन̍ य̱ज्ञम̍यजन्त दे̱वास्तानि̱ धर्मा̍णि प्रथ̱मान्या̍सन् ते ह̱ नाक̍ं महि̱मान̍: सचन्त̱ यत्र̱ पूर्वे̍ सा̱ध्याः सन्ति̍ दे̱वाः
296.m: With sacrifice the gods sacrificed to sacrifice: these were the first ordinances. / These mighty ones attained the firmament, where the ancient Sādhyas and gods dwell.

297.s: (1) a̱dbhyaḥ saṃbhū̍taḥ pṛthi̱vyai rasā̍cca vi̱śvaka̍rmaṇa̱ḥ sama̍varta̱tāgre̍ tasya̱ tvaṣṭā̍ vi̱dadha̍drū̱pame̍ti̱ tanmartya̍sya deva̱tvamā̱jāna̱magre̍
297.d: (1) अ̱द्भ्यः संभू̍तः पृथि̱व्यै रसा̍च्च वि̱श्वक̍र्मण̱ः सम̍वर्त̱ताग्रे̍ तस्य̱ त्वष्टा̍ वि̱दध̍द्रू̱पमे̍ति̱ तन्मर्त्य̍स्य देव̱त्वमा̱जान̱मग्रे̍
297.m: Gathered from the waters, from the earth, and from the sap of Viśvakarman, he evolved in the beginning. / Tvaṣṭṛ goes shaping his form; that was the divinity of the mortal, his birth in the beginning.

297.s: vedā̱hame̱taṃ puru̍ṣaṃ ma̱hānta̍mādi̱tyava̍rṇa̱ṃ tama̍saḥ pa̱rastā̍t tame̱va vi̍di̱tvāti̍ mṛ̱tyume̍ti̱ nānyaḥ panthā̍ vidyate'ya̍nāya
297.d: वेदा̱हमे̱तं पुरु̍षं म̱हान्त̍मादि̱त्यव̍र्ण̱ं तम̍सः प̱रस्ता̍त् तमे̱व वि̍दि̱त्वाति̍ मृ̱त्युमे̍ति̱ नान्यः पन्था̍ विद्यतेऽय̍नाय
297.m: I know this great Person, of sun-like color, beyond darkness. / Knowing him alone, one goes beyond death; there is no other path for going.

297.s: pra̱jāpa̍tiścarati̱ garbhe̍ a̱ntarajā̍yamāno bahu̱dhā vi jā̍yate tasya̱ yoni̱ṃ pari̍ paśyanti̱ dhīrā̱stasmi̍nha tasthu̱rbhuva̍nāni̱ viśvā̍
297.d: प्र̱जाप̍तिश्चरति̱ गर्भे̍ अ̱न्तरजा̍यमानो बहु̱धा वि जा̍यते तस्य̱ योनि̱ं परि̍ पश्यन्ति̱ धीरा̱स्तस्मि̍न्ह तस्थु̱र्भुव̍नानि̱ विश्वा̍
297.m: Prajāpati moves within the womb; unborn, he is born manifoldly. / The wise gaze upon his source; in him all beings have stood firm.

297.s: yo de̱vebhya̍ ātapa̍ti̱ yo de̱vānā̍ṃ purohi̍taḥ pūrvo̱ yo de̱vebhyo̍ jā̱to namo̍ ru̱cāya̱ brāhma̍ye
297.d: यो दे̱वेभ्य̍ आतप̍ति̱ यो दे̱वाना̍ं पुरोहि̍तः पूर्वो̱ यो दे̱वेभ्यो̍ जा̱तो नमो̍ रु̱चाय̱ ब्राह्म̍ये
297.m: He who shines forth for the gods, who is the purohita of the gods, / who was born prior to the gods—homage to the radiant, Brahman-related one!

297.s: ruca̍ṃ brā̱hmaṃ ja̱naya̍nto de̱vā agre̱ tada̍bruvan yastvai̱vaṃ brā̍hma̱ṇo vi̱dyāttasya̍ de̱vā asa̱nvaśe̍
297.d: रुच̍ं ब्रा̱ह्मं ज̱नय̍न्तो दे̱वा अग्रे̱ तद̍ब्रुवन् यस्त्वै̱वं ब्रा̍ह्म̱णो वि̱द्यात्तस्य̍ दे̱वा अस̱न्वशे̍
297.m: Generating the radiant, Brahman-related one, the gods spoke thus in the beginning: / "The brāhmaṇa who shall know you thus, the gods will be in his control."

297.s: śrīśca̍ te la̱kṣmīśca̱ patnyā̍vahorā̱tre pā̱rśve nakṣa̍trāṇi rū̱pama̱śvinau̱ vyātta̍m i̱ṣṇanni̍ṣāṇā̱muṃ ma̍ iṣāṇa sarvalo̱kaṃ ma̍ iṣāṇa
297.d: श्रीश्च̍ ते ल̱क्ष्मीश्च̱ पत्न्या̍वहोरा̱त्रे पा̱र्श्वे नक्ष̍त्राणि रू̱पम̱श्विनौ̱ व्यात्त̍म् इ̱ष्णन्नि̍षाणा̱मुं म̍ इषाण सर्वलो̱कं म̍ इषाण
297.m: Śrī and Lakṣmī are your wives; day and night your sides; the constellations your form; the two Aśvins your wide-open mouth. / Urging, urge this for me; urge for me the entire world.

298.s: (2) tade̱vāgnistadā̍di̱tyastadvā̱yustadu̍ ca̱ndramā̍: tade̱va śu̱kraṃ tad brahma̱ tadāpa̍: tatpra̱jāpa̍tiḥ
298.d: (2) तदे̱वाग्निस्तदा̍दि̱त्यस्तद्वा̱युस्तदु̍ च̱न्द्रमा̍: तदे̱व शु̱क्रं तद् ब्रह्म̱ तदाप̍: तत्प्र̱जाप̍तिः
298.m: That alone is Agni, that Āditya, that Vāyu, that too the moon; / that alone is the bright, that Brahman, that the waters, that Prajāpati.

298.s: sarve̍ nime̱ṣā ja̍jñire vi̱dyuta̍: puru̍ṣā̱dadhi̍ naina̍mū̱rdhvaṃ na ti̱ryañca̱ṃ na madhye̱ pari̍ jagrabhat
298.d: सर्वे̍ निमे̱षा ज̍ज्ञिरे वि̱द्युत̍: पुरु̍षा̱दधि̍ नैन̍मू̱र्ध्वं न ति̱र्यञ्च̱ं न मध्ये̱ परि̍ जग्रभत्
298.m: All twinking instants were born from lightning, from above the Person. / None has grasped him above, nor across, nor in the middle.

298.s: na tasya̍ prati̱mā a̍sti̱ yasya̱ nāma̍ ma̱hadyaśa̍: hiraṇyagarbha ityeṣaḥ
298.d: न तस्य̍ प्रति̱मा अ̍स्ति̱ यस्य̱ नाम̍ म̱हद्यश̍: हिरण्यगर्भ इत्येषः
298.m: There is no likeness of him whose name is great glory. / "The Golden Embryo"—this is he.

298.s: e̱ṣo ha̍ de̱vaḥ pra̱diśo'nu̱ sarvā̍: pūrvo̍ ha jā̱taḥ sa u̱ garbhe̍ a̱ntaḥ sa e̱va jā̱taḥ sa ja̍niṣyamā̍ṇaḥ pra̱tyaṅ janā̍stiṣṭhati sarvato̍mukhaḥ yasmānna jāta ityeṣaḥ
298.d: ए̱षो ह̍ दे̱वः प्र̱दिशोऽनु̱ सर्वा̍: पूर्वो̍ ह जा̱तः स उ̱ गर्भे̍ अ̱न्तः स ए̱व जा̱तः स ज̍निष्यमा̍णः प्र̱त्यङ् जना̍स्तिष्ठति सर्वतो̍मुखः यस्मान्न जात इत्येषः
298.m: This god is along all the intermediate quarters; born of old, he is inside the womb. / He indeed is born, he is about to be born; facing inward toward creatures, he stands with faces on all sides. / "From whom none was born"—this is he.

298.s: ve̱nastatpa̍śya̱nnihi̍ta̱ṃ guhā̱ sadyatra̱ viśva̱ṃ bhava̱tyeka̍nīḷam tasmi̍nni̱dam̐ saṃ ca̱ vi cai̍ti̱ sarva̱m̐ sa ota̱ḥ prota̍śca vi̱bhūḥ pra̱jāsu̍
298.d: वे̱नस्तत्प̍श्य̱न्निहि̍त̱ं गुहा̱ सद्यत्र̱ विश्व̱ं भव̱त्येक̍नीऌअम् तस्मि̍न्नि̱दम्̐ सं च̱ वि चै̍ति̱ सर्व̱म्̐ स ओत̱ः प्रोत̍श्च वि̱भूः प्र̱जासु̍
298.m: Vena, seeing that which is placed in secret, where the universe becomes of one single nest, / in that this all comes together and dissolves; he is the warp and the woof, all-pervading in creatures.

298.s: pra tadvo̍cedamṛ̱taṃ nu vi̱dvānga̍ndha̱rvo dhāma̱ vibhṛ̍ta̱ṃ guhā̱ sat trīṇi̍ pa̱dāni̱ nihi̍tā̱ guhā̍sya̱ yastāni̱ veda̱ sa pi̱tuḥ pi̱tāsa̍t
298.d: प्र तद्वो̍चेदमृ̱तं नु वि̱द्वान्ग̍न्ध̱र्वो धाम̱ विभृ̍त̱ं गुहा̱ सत् त्रीणि̍ प̱दानि̱ निहि̍ता̱ गुहा̍स्य̱ यस्तानि̱ वेद̱ स पि̱तुः पि̱तास̍त्
298.m: Let the Gandharva, now knowing the immortal, proclaim that abode hidden in secret. / Three steps of his are placed in secret; he who knows them shall be the father of the father.

298.s: sa no bandhu̍rjani̱tā sa vi̍dhā̱tā dhāmā̍ni̱ veda̱ bhuva̍nāni̱ viśvā̍ yatra̍ de̱vā a̱mṛta̍mānaśā̱nāstṛ̱tīye̱ dhāma̍nna̱dhyaira̍yanta
298.d: स नो बन्धु̍र्जनि̱ता स वि̍धा̱ता धामा̍नि̱ वेद̱ भुव̍नानि̱ विश्वा̍ यत्र̍ दे̱वा अ̱मृत̍मानशा̱नास्तृ̱तीये̱ धाम̍न्न̱ध्यैर̍यन्त
298.m: He is our kinsman, begetter, he the disposer; he knows the abodes, all the worlds, / where the gods, having attained immortality, moved upward in the third abode.

298.s: parītya̍ bhū̱tāni̍ pa̱rītya̍ lo̱kānparītya̱ sarvā̍ḥ pra̱diśo̱ diśa̍śca u̱pa̱sthāya̍ prathama̱jāmṛ̱tasyā̱tmanā̱tmāna̍ma̱bhi saṃ vi̍veśa
298.d: परीत्य̍ भू̱तानि̍ प̱रीत्य̍ लो̱कान्परीत्य̱ सर्वा̍ः प्र̱दिशो̱ दिश̍श्च उ̱प̱स्थाय̍ प्रथम̱जामृ̱तस्या̱त्मना̱त्मान̍म̱भि सं वि̍वेश
298.m: Having gone around beings, having gone around the worlds, having gone around all the intermediate quarters and the directions, / having approached the firstborn of truth, through himself he entered into himself.

298.s: pari̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī sa̱dya i̱tvā pari̍ lo̱kānpari̱ diśa̱ḥ pari̱ sva̍ḥ ṛ̱tasya̱ tantu̍ṃ vi̱tata̍ṃ vi̱cṛtya̱ tada̍paśya̱ttada̍bhava̱ttadā̍sīt
298.d: परि̱ द्यावा̍पृथि̱वी स̱द्य इ̱त्वा परि̍ लो̱कान्परि̱ दिश̱ः परि̱ स्व̍ः ऋ̱तस्य̱ तन्तु̍ं वि̱तत̍ं वि̱चृत्य̱ तद̍पश्य̱त्तद̍भव̱त्तदा̍सीत्
298.m: Having immediately gone around heaven and earth, around the worlds, around the directions, around heaven, / untying the stretched thread of truth, he saw that, he became that, he was that.

298.s: sada̍sa̱spati̱madbhu̍taṃ pri̱yamindra̍sya̱ kāmya̍m | sa̱niṃ me̱dhāma̍yāsiṣam̐ svāhā̍
298.d: सद̍स̱स्पति̱मद्भु̍तं प्रि̱यमिन्द्र̍स्य̱ काम्य̍म् । स̱निं मे̱धाम̍यासिषम्̐ स्वाहा̍
298.m: To Sadasaspati, the wondrous, dear to Indra, desirable, / the prize, wisdom have I sought, svāhā!

298.s: yāṃ me̱dhāṃ de̍vaga̱ṇāḥ pi̱tara̍śco̱pāsa̍te | tayā̱ māma̱dya me̱dhayāgne̍ me̱dhāvi̍naṃ kuru̱ svāhā̍
298.d: यां मे̱धां दे̍वग̱णाः पि̱तर̍श्चो̱पास̍ते । तया̱ माम̱द्य मे̱धयाग्ने̍ मे̱धावि̍नं कुरु̱ स्वाहा̍
298.m: The wisdom which the hosts of gods and the fathers revere, / with that wisdom make me wise today, Agni, svāhā!

298.s: i̱daṃ me̱ brahma̍ ca kṣa̱traṃ co̱bhe śriya̍maśnutām mayi̍ de̱vā da̍dhatu̱ śriya̍mutta̱māṃ tasyai̍ te̱ svāhā̍
298.d: इ̱दं मे̱ ब्रह्म̍ च क्ष̱त्रं चो̱भे श्रिय̍मश्नुताम् मयि̍ दे̱वा द̍धतु̱ श्रिय̍मुत्त̱मां तस्यै̍ ते̱ स्वाहा̍
298.m: May both my Brahman and princely power attain glory. / May the gods place supreme glory in me. To that [glory] of yours, svāhā!

299.s: ape̍to ya̍ntu pa̱ṇayo̍'su̱ṃmnā de̍vapī̱yava̍ḥ | a̱sya lo̱kaḥ su̱tāva̍taḥ
299.d: अपे̍तो य̍न्तु प̱णयो̍ऽसु̱ंम्ना दे̍वपी̱यव̍ः । अ̱स्य लो̱कः सु̱ताव̍तः
299.m: Let the Panis, the ungracious, the revilers of gods, depart from here. / This world belongs to him who presses [Soma].

299.s: dyu̱bhirho̍bhi̱raktubhi̱rvya̍ktaṃ ya̱mo da̍dātvava̱sāna̍masmai sa̱vi̱tā te̱ śarī̍rebhyaḥ pṛthi̱vyām̐ lo̱kami̍cchatu | tasmai̍ yujyantāmu̱sriyā̍ḥ
299.d: द्यु̱भिर्हो̍भि̱रक्तुभि̱र्व्य̍क्तं य̱मो द̍दात्वव̱सान̍मस्मै स̱वि̱ता ते̱ शरी̍रेभ्यः पृथि̱व्याम्̐ लो̱कमि̍च्छतु । तस्मै̍ युज्यन्तामु̱स्रिया̍ः
299.m: May Yama give an abode to him, made clear by skies, days, and nights. / May Savitṛ seek a place on earth for your bones. May the reddish cows be yoked for him.

299.s: vā̱yuḥ pu̍nātu savi̱tā pu̍nātva̱gnerbhrāja̍sā sūrya̍sya̱ varca̍sā | vi mu̍cyantāmu̱sriyā̍ḥ
299.d: वा̱युः पु̍नातु सवि̱ता पु̍नात्व̱ग्नेर्भ्राज̍सा सूर्य̍स्य̱ वर्च̍सा । वि मु̍च्यन्तामु̱स्रिया̍ः
299.m: May Vāyu purify, may Savitṛ purify with the brilliance of Agni, with the splendor of the sun. May the reddish cows be unyoked.

299.s: a̱śva̱tthe vo̍ ni̱ṣada̍naṃ pa̱rṇe vo̍ vasa̱tiṣkṛ̱tā | go̱bhāja̱ itkilāsa̍tha̱ yatsa̱nava̍tha̱ pūru̍ṣam
299.d: अ̱श्व̱त्थे वो̍ नि̱षद̍नं प̱र्णे वो̍ वस̱तिष्कृ̱ता । गो̱भाज̱ इत्किलास̍थ̱ यत्स̱नव̍थ̱ पूरु̍षम्
299.m: In the aśvattha is your seat; in the parṇa your dwelling is made. / Cattle-sharers indeed shall you be, when you win the man.

299.s: savi̱tā te̱ śarī̍rāṇi mā̱turu̱pastha̱ ā va̍patu | tasmai̍ pṛthi̱vi śaṃ bha̍va pra̱jāpa̍tau tvā de̱vatā̍yāmu̱poda̍ke lo̱ke ni da̍dhāmya̱sau
299.d: सवि̱ता ते̱ शरी̍राणि मा̱तुरु̱पस्थ̱ आ व̍पतु । तस्मै̍ पृथि̱वि शं भ̍व प्र̱जाप̍तौ त्वा दे̱वता̍यामु̱पोद̍के लो̱के नि द̍धाम्य̱सौ
299.m: May Savitṛ deposit your bones into the lap of the mother. Be auspicious to him, O earth. / In Prajāpati, as deity, in the watery world I place you, N.N.

299.s: para̍ṃ mṛtyo̱ anu̱ pare̍hi̱ panthā̱ṃ yaste̱ anya ita̍ro deva̱yānā̍t cakṣu̍ṣmate śṛṇva̱te te̍ bravīmi̱ mā na̍ḥ pra̱jām̐ rī̍riṣo̱ mota vī̱rān
299.d: पर̍ं मृत्यो̱ अनु̱ परे̍हि̱ पन्था̱ं यस्ते̱ अन्य इत̍रो देव̱याना̍त् चक्षु̍ष्मते शृण्व̱ते ते̍ ब्रवीमि̱ मा न̍ः प्र̱जाम्̐ री̍रिषो̱ मोत वी̱रान्
299.m: Follow a further path, O death, which is yours, other and distinct from the path of the gods. / To you who see and hear I speak: do not harm our offspring, nor our heroes.

299.s: śaṃ vāta̍ḥ śam̐ hi te̱ ghṛṇi̍ḥ śaṃ te̍ bhavantviṣṭa̍kāḥ śaṃ te̍ bhavantva̱gnaya̱ḥ pārthi̍vāso̱ mā tvā̱bhi śū̍śucan
299.d: शं वात̍ः शम्̐ हि ते̱ घृणि̍ः शं ते̍ भवन्त्विष्ट̍काः शं ते̍ भवन्त्व̱ग्नय̱ः पार्थि̍वासो̱ मा त्वा̱भि शू̍शुचन्
299.m: Auspicious be the wind, auspicious indeed to you the heat; auspicious to you be the bricks. / Auspicious to you be the earthly fires; let them not cause you grief.

299.s: kalpa̍ntāṃ te̱ diśa̱stubhya̱māpa̍ḥ śi̱vata̍māstubhya̍ṃ bhavantu sindha̍vaḥ a̱ntari̍kṣam̐ śi̱vaṃ tubhya̱ṃ kalpa̍ntāṃ te̱ diśa̱ḥ sarvā̍ḥ
299.d: कल्प̍न्तां ते̱ दिश̱स्तुभ्य̱माप̍ः शि̱वत̍मास्तुभ्य̍ं भवन्तु सिन्ध̍वः अ̱न्तरि̍क्षम्̐ शि̱वं तुभ्य̱ं कल्प̍न्तां ते̱ दिश̱ः सर्वा̍ः
299.m: May the directions be arranged for you; may the waters be most auspicious for you, auspicious for you the rivers. / May the mid-air be auspicious for you; may all the directions be arranged for you.

299.s: aśma̍nvatī rīyate̱ sam̐ ra̍bhadhva̱mutti̍ṣṭhata̱ pra ta̍ratā sakhāyaḥ atrā̍ jahīmo̱'śivā̱ ye asa̱ñchivānva̱yamutta̍re̱mābhi vājā̍n
299.d: अश्म̍न्वती रीयते̱ सम्̐ र̍भध्व̱मुत्ति̍ष्ठत̱ प्र त̍रता सखायः अत्रा̍ जहीमो̱ऽशिवा̱ ये अस̱ञ्छिवान्व̱यमुत्त̍रे̱माभि वाजा̍न्
299.m: The stony [river] flows; hold together, stand up, cross over, friends! / Here let us leave those that are inauspicious; let us cross over to auspicious vital vigors!

299.s: apā̍ghamapa̍ kilbi̍ṣa̱mapa̍ kṛ̱tyāmapo̱ rapa̍ḥ apā̍mā̱rga̱ tvama̱smadapa̍ duḥṣva̱pnyam̐̍ suva
299.d: अपा̍घमप̍ किल्बि̍ष̱मप̍ कृ̱त्यामपो̱ रप̍ः अपा̍मा̱र्ग̱ त्वम̱स्मदप̍ दुःष्व̱प्न्यम्̐̍ सुव
299.m: Away [drive] evil, away sin, away sorcery, away disease! / O apāmārga-plant, drive bad dreams away from us!

299.s: su̱mi̱tri̱yā na̱ āpa̱ oṣa̍dhayaḥ santu durmitri̱yāstasmai̍ santu yo̱'smāndveṣṭi̱ yaṃ ca̍ va̱yaṃ dvi̱ṣmaḥ
299.d: सु̱मि̱त्रि̱या न̱ आप̱ ओष̍धयः सन्तु दुर्मित्रि̱यास्तस्मै̍ सन्तु यो̱ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि̱ यं च̍ व̱यं द्वि̱ष्मः
299.m: May the waters, the plants, be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him / who hates us and whom we hate.

299.s: a̱na̱ḍvāha̱manvā̍rabhāmahe sva̱stayai̍ sa na̱ indra̍ iva de̱vebhyo̱ vahni̍ḥ sa̱ṃtāra̍ṇo bhava
299.d: अ̱न̱ड्वाह̱मन्वा̍रभामहे स्व̱स्तयै̍ स न̱ इन्द्र̍ इव दे̱वेभ्यो̱ वह्नि̍ः स̱ंतार̍णो भव
299.m: We take hold of the draft-ox for well-being. / Like Indra for the gods, be you our draft-carrier, taking us across.

299.s: udva̱yaṃ tama̍sa̱spari̱ svaḥ paśya̍nta̱ utta̍ram de̱vaṃ de̍va̱trā sūrya̱maga̍nma̱ jyoti̍rutta̱mam
299.d: उद्व̱यं तम̍स̱स्परि̱ स्वः पश्य̍न्त̱ उत्त̍रम् दे̱वं दे̍व̱त्रा सूर्य̱मग̍न्म̱ ज्योति̍रुत्त̱मम्
299.m: Looking up beyond darkness to the higher heaven, / we have come to Sūrya, a god among gods, the highest light.

299.s: agna̱ āyū̍m̐ṣi pavasa̱ ā suvorja̱miṣa̍ṃ ca naḥ āre bā̍dhasva du̱cchunā̍m
299.d: अग्न̱ आयू̍म्̐षि पवस̱ आ सुवोर्ज̱मिष̍ं च नः आरे बा̍धस्व दु̱च्छुना̍म्
299.m: O Agni, you purify life; bring us sap and refreshment; / drive afar distress.

299.s: āyu̍ṣmānagne ha̱viṣā̍ vṛdhā̱no ghṛ̱tapra̍tīko ghṛ̱tayo̍niredhi ghṛ̱taṃ pī̱tvā madhu̱ cāru̱ gavya̍ṃ pi̱teva̍ pu̱trama̱bhi ra̍kṣatādi̱māntsvāhā̍
299.d: आयु̍ष्मानग्ने ह̱विषा̍ वृधा̱नो घृ̱तप्र̍तीको घृ̱तयो̍निरेधि घृ̱तं पी̱त्वा मधु̱ चारु̱ गव्य̍ं पि̱तेव̍ पु̱त्रम̱भि र̍क्षतादि̱मान्त्स्वाहा̍
299.m: Long-lived, O Agni, growing through oblation, with ghee for your face and ghee for your womb, / having drunk ghee, the sweet, lovely [produce] of cattle, protect these like a father his son, svāhā!

299.s: i̱maṃ jī̱vebhya̍ḥ pari̱dhiṃ da̍dhāmi̱ maiṣā̱ṃ nu gādapa̍ro̱ artha̍me̱tam śa̱taṃ jī̍vantu śa̱rada̍ḥ purū̱cīra̱ntarmṛ̱tyuṃ da̍dhatā̱ṃ parva̍tena
299.d: इ̱मं जी̱वेभ्य̍ः परि̱धिं द̍धामि̱ मैषा̱ं नु गादप̍रो̱ अर्थ̍मे̱तम् श̱तं जी̍वन्तु श̱रद̍ः पुरू̱चीर̱न्तर्मृ̱त्युं द̍धता̱ं पर्व̍तेन
299.m: I place this perimeter for the living: let not another of them go now to this goal; / may they live for a hundred full autumns, setting death aside with a rock.

299.s: parī̱me gāma̍neṣata̱ parya̱gnima̍hṛṣata | de̱veṣva̍krata̱ śrava̍ḥ ka i̱mām̐2 ā da̍dharṣati
299.d: परी̱मे गाम̍नेषत̱ पर्य̱ग्निम̍हृषत । दे̱वेष्व̍क्रत̱ श्रव̍ः क इ̱माम्̐2 आ द̍धर्षति
299.m: These have led round the cow, they have carried fire around, / they have won fame among the gods: who will dare attack them?

299.s: kra̱vyāda̍ma̱gniṃ pra hi̍ṇomi dū̱raṃ ya̍ma̱rājya̍ṃ gacchatu ripravā̱haḥ i̱haivāyamita̍ro jā̱tave̍dā de̱vebhyo̍ ha̱vyaṃ va̍hatu prajā̱nan
299.d: क्र̱व्याद̍म̱ग्निं प्र हि̍णोमि दू̱रं य̍म̱राज्य̍ं गच्छतु रिप्रवा̱हः इ̱हैवायमित̍रो जा̱तवे̍दा दे̱वेभ्यो̍ ह̱व्यं व̍हतु प्रजा̱नन्
299.m: I send far away the flesh-devouring fire; carrying stain, let it go to the realm of Yama; / let this other Jātavedas right here, knowing well, carry the oblation to the gods.

299.s: vaha̍ vapāṃ jātavedaḥ pi̱tṛbhyo̱ yatrai̍nānvettha̱ nihi̍tānparā̱ke meda̍saḥ ku̱lyā upa̱ tāntsra̍vantu sa̱tyā e̍ṣāmā̱śiṣa̍ḥ santu̱ kāmā̱ḥ svāhā̍
299.d: वह̍ वपां जातवेदः पि̱तृभ्यो̱ यत्रै̍नान्वेत्थ̱ निहि̍तान्परा̱के मेद̍सः कु̱ल्या उप̱ तान्त्स्र̍वन्तु स̱त्या ए̍षामा̱शिष̍ः सन्तु̱ कामा̱ः स्वाहा̍
299.m: Carry the omentum, O Jātavedas, to the fathers where you know they are placed far away; / may channels of fat flow to them; let their prayers and wishes come true, svāhā!

299.s: syo̱nā pṛ̍thivi no bhavā̱nṛkṣa̱rā ni̱veśa̍nī yacchā̍ na̱ḥ śarma̍ sa̱prathā̍ḥ | apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cada̱gham
299.d: स्यो̱ना पृ̍थिवि नो भवा̱नृक्ष̱रा नि̱वेश̍नी यच्छा̍ न̱ः शर्म̍ स̱प्रथा̍ः । अप̍ न̱ः शोशु̍चद̱घम्
299.m: Be pleasant to us, O earth, thornless and a peaceful resting-place; / grant us wide refuge; burn away our sin.

299.s:
a̱smāttvamadhi̍ jā̱to̍'si̱ tvada̱yaṃ jā̍yatā̱ṃ puna̍ḥ | a̱sau sva̱rgāya̍ lo̱kāya̱ svāhā̍ apa̍ na̱ḥ śośu̍cada̱gham
(4) sahasraśīrṣā ṣoḍaśa
aṅgadhaḥ saṃbhṛtaḥ ṣaṭ
tadevāgnirdvādaśa
apeto yantvekaviṃśatiḥ
299.d:
अ̱स्मात्त्वमधि̍ जा̱तो̍ऽसि̱ त्वद̱यं जा̍यता̱ं पुन̍ः । अ̱सौ स्व̱र्गाय̍ लो̱काय̱ स्वाहा̍ अप̍ न̱ः शोशु̍चद̱घम्
(4) सहस्रशीर्षा षोडश
अङ्गधः संभृतः षट्
तदेवाग्निर्द्वादश
अपेतो यन्त्वेकविंशतिः
299.m:
From him you were born; let this one be born again from you / for that heavenly world, svāhā! / Burn away our sin.

[The hymn] 'Thousand-headed' has sixteen [verses]; 'Brought together from the waters' has six; 'That very one is Agni' has twelve; / 'Let them go away' has twenty-one; in the four sections there are fifty-five. / Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter in the Śukla Yajurveda Kāṇva Saṃhitā.

299.s: caturanuvākeṣu pañcapañcāśat
299.d: चतुरनुवाकेषु पञ्चपञ्चाशत्

300.s: ṛ̱caṃ vāca̱ṃ pra pa̍dye̱ mano̱ yaju̱ḥ pra pa̍dye̱ sāma̍ prā̱ṇaṃ pra pa̍dye̱ cakṣu̱ḥ śrotra̱ṃ pra pa̍dye vāgoja̍: sa̱haujo mayi̍ prāṇāpā̱nau
300.d: ऋ̱चं वाच̱ं प्र प̍द्ये̱ मनो̱ यजु̱ः प्र प̍द्ये̱ साम̍ प्रा̱णं प्र प̍द्ये̱ चक्षु̱ः श्रोत्र̱ं प्र प̍द्ये वागोज̍: स̱हौजो मयि̍ प्राणापा̱नौ
300.m: I take refuge in verse and speech; I take refuge in mind and the sacrificial formula; I take refuge in chant and in-breath; I take refuge in sight and hearing. / Speech, strength, power, and vigour be in me, in-breath and out-breath.

300.s: yanme̍ chi̱draṃ cakṣu̍ṣo̱ hṛda̍yasya̱ mana̍so vāti̍tṛ̱ṇṇaṃ bṛha̱spati̍rme̱ tadda̍dhātu śaṃ no̍ bhavatu bhuva̍nasya̱ yaspati̍:
300.d: यन्मे̍ छि̱द्रं चक्षु̍षो̱ हृद̍यस्य̱ मन̍सो वाति̍तृ̱ण्णं बृह̱स्पति̍र्मे̱ तद्द̍धातु शं नो̍ भवतु भुव̍नस्य̱ यस्पति̍:
300.m: Whatever flaw of my eye, heart, or mind has been torn open, may Bṛhaspati mend that for me; / may he who is the protector of the world be gracious to us.

300.s: bhūrbhuva̱ḥ sva̍ḥ | tatsa̍vi̱turvare̍ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̍t
300.d: भूर्भुव̱ः स्व̍ः । तत्स̍वि̱तुर्वरे̍ण्य̱ं भर्गो̍ दे̱वस्य̍ धीमहि । धियो̱ यो न̍ः प्रचो̱दया̍त्
300.m: Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ. Let us meditate on that excellent splendor of god Savitṛ, / who may inspire our visions.

300.s: kayā̍ naści̱tra ā bhu̍vadū̱tī sa̱dāvṛ̍dhaḥ sakhā̍ | kayā̱ śaci̍ṣṭhayā vṛ̱tā
300.d: कया̍ नश्चि̱त्र आ भु̍वदू̱ती स̱दावृ̍धः सखा̍ । कया̱ शचि̍ष्ठया वृ̱ता
300.m: With what aid will the wondrous friend, ever prospering, be with us? / With what most powerful assistance?

300.s: kastvā̍ sa̱tyo madā̍nā̱ṃ maṃhi̍ṣṭho matsadandha̍saḥ | dṛ̱ḷhā ci̍dāru̱je vasu̍
300.d: कस्त्वा̍ स̱त्यो मदा̍ना̱ं मंहि̍ष्ठो मत्सदन्ध̍सः । दृ̱ऌहा चि̍दारु̱जे वसु̍
300.m: What truest, most generous exhilaration of the drinks will exhilarate you / to break through even solid strongholds [and bring] wealth?

300.s: a̱bhī ṣu ṇa̱ḥ sakhī̍nāmavi̱tā ja̍ritṝ̱ṇām | śa̱taṃ bha̍vāsyū̱tibhi̍:
300.d: अ̱भी षु ण̱ः सखी̍नामवि̱ता ज̍रितॄ̱णाम् । श̱तं भ̍वास्यू̱तिभि̍:
300.m: Be the protector of us, your friends and singers, / with a hundred aids.

300.s: kayā̱ tvaṃ na̍ ū̱tyābhi pra ma̍ṃndase vṛṣan | kayā̍ sto̱tṛbhya̱ ā bha̍ra
300.d: कया̱ त्वं न̍ ऊ̱त्याभि प्र म̍ंन्दसे वृषन् । कया̍ स्तो̱तृभ्य̱ आ भ̍र
300.m: With what aid, O bull, do you take pleasure in us? / With what do you bring [wealth] to the praisers?

300.s: indro̱ viśva̍sya rājati | śaṃ no̍ astu dvi̱pade̱ śaṃ catu̍ṣpade
300.d: इन्द्रो̱ विश्व̍स्य राजति । शं नो̍ अस्तु द्वि̱पदे̱ शं चतु̍ष्पदे
300.m: Indra rules over all; / may there be well-being for our two-footed and well-being for our four-footed [creatures].

300.s: śaṃ no̍ mi̱traḥ śaṃ varu̍ṇa̱ḥ śaṃ no̍ bhavatvarya̱mā | śaṃ na̱ indro̱ bṛha̱spati̱ḥ śaṃ no̱ viṣṇu̍rurukra̱maḥ
300.d: शं नो̍ मि̱त्रः शं वरु̍ण̱ः शं नो̍ भवत्वर्य̱मा । शं न̱ इन्द्रो̱ बृह̱स्पति̱ः शं नो̱ विष्णु̍रुरुक्र̱मः
300.m: May Mitra bring us peace, may Varuṇa bring us peace, may Aryaman be peace to us; / may Indra and Bṛhaspati bring us peace; may wide-striding Viṣṇu bring us peace.

300.s: śaṃ no̱ vāta̍ḥ pavatā̱m̐ śaṃ na̍stapatu sūrya̍: | śaṃ na̱ḥ kani̍kradadde̱vaḥ pa̱rjanyo̍ a̱bhi va̍rṣatu
300.d: शं नो̱ वात̍ः पवता̱म्̐ शं न̍स्तपतु सूर्य̍: । शं न̱ः कनि̍क्रदद्दे̱वः प̱र्जन्यो̍ अ̱भि व̍र्षतु
300.m: May the wind blow peace to us, may Sūrya radiate peace to us; / may the god Parjanya, roaring, rain peace down upon us.

300.s: ahā̍ni̱ śaṃ bha̍vantu na̱ḥ śam̐ rātrī̱ḥ prati̍ dhīyatām śaṃ na̍ indrā̱gnī bha̍vatāmavo̍bhi̱ḥ śaṃ na̱ indrāvaru̍ṇā rātaha̍vyā śaṃ na̍ indrāpū̱ṣaṇā̱ vāja̍sātau̱ śamindrāsomā̍ suvi̱tāya̱ śaṃ yoḥ
300.d: अहा̍नि̱ शं भ̍वन्तु न̱ः शम्̐ रात्री̱ः प्रति̍ धीयताम् शं न̍ इन्द्रा̱ग्नी भ̍वतामवो̍भि̱ः शं न̱ इन्द्रावरु̍णा रातह̍व्या शं न̍ इन्द्रापू̱षणा̱ वाज̍सातौ̱ शमिन्द्रासोमा̍ सुवि̱ताय̱ शं योः
300.m: May the days be peaceful to us, may the nights bring peace; / may Indrāgnī bring us peace with aids; may Indrāvaruṇā, receiving our oblations, bring us peace; / may Indrāpūṣan bring peace at the winning of vital vigor; may Indrāsoma bring peace and good fortune, welfare and blessing.

300.s: śaṃ no̍ de̱vīra̱bhiṣṭa̍ya̱ āpo̍ bhavantu pī̱taye̍ | śaṃ yora̱bhi sra̍vantu naḥ
300.d: शं नो̍ दे̱वीर̱भिष्ट̍य̱ आपो̍ भवन्तु पी̱तये̍ । शं योर̱भि स्र̍वन्तु नः
300.m: May the divine waters bring peace for our aid and for drinking; / may they flow peace and blessing to us.

300.s: syo̱nā pṛ̍thivi no bhavā̱nṛkṣa̱rā ni̱veśa̍nī | yacchā̍ na̱ḥ śarma̍ sa̱prathā̍:
300.d: स्यो̱ना पृ̍थिवि नो भवा̱नृक्ष̱रा नि̱वेश̍नी । यच्छा̍ न̱ः शर्म̍ स̱प्रथा̍:
300.m: Be pleasant to us, O earth, thornless and a peaceful resting-place; / grant us wide refuge.

300.s: āpo̱ hi ṣṭhā ma̍yo̱bhuva̱stā na̍ ū̱rje da̍dhātana | ma̱he raṇā̍ya̱ cakṣa̍se
300.d: आपो̱ हि ष्ठा म̍यो̱भुव̱स्ता न̍ ऊ̱र्जे द̍धातन । म̱हे रणा̍य̱ चक्ष̍से
300.m: Since you, waters, are soothing, bestow upon us vital strength, / so that we may look upon great joy.

300.s: yo va̍ḥ śi̱vata̍mo rasa̱stasya̍ bhājayate̱ha na̍ḥ | u̱śa̱tīri̍va mā̱tara̍:
300.d: यो व̍ः शि̱वत̍मो रस̱स्तस्य̍ भाजयते̱ह न̍ः । उ̱श̱तीरि̍व मा̱तर̍:
300.m: Whatever most auspicious sap is yours, make us share in it here, / like eager mothers.

300.s: tasmā̱ ara̍ṃ gamāma vo̱ yasya̱ kṣayā̍ya̱ jinva̍tha | āpo̍ ja̱naya̍thā ca naḥ
300.d: तस्मा̱ अर̍ं गमाम वो̱ यस्य̱ क्षया̍य̱ जिन्व̍थ । आपो̍ ज̱नय̍था च नः
300.m: Let us quickly go to that [abode] of yours for whose domain you refresh us; / and, O waters, generate us anew.

300.s: dyauḥ śānti̍ra̱ntari̍kṣa̱m̐ śānti̍ḥ pṛthi̱vī śānti̱rāpa̱ḥ śānti̱roṣa̍dhaya̱ḥ śānti̍: vana̱spata̍ya̱ḥ śānti̱: śānti̍re̱va śānti̍:
300.d: द्यौः शान्ति̍र̱न्तरि̍क्ष̱म्̐ शान्ति̍ः पृथि̱वी शान्ति̱राप̱ः शान्ति̱रोष̍धय̱ः शान्ति̍: वन̱स्पत̍य̱ः शान्ति̱: शान्ति̍रे̱व शान्ति̍:
300.m: Heaven is peace, mid-air is peace, earth is peace, the waters are peace, the plants are peace, / the trees of the forest are peace, peace itself is peace.

300.s: dṛ̱te dṛm̐ha̍ mā mi̱trasya̍ mā̱ cakṣu̍ṣā sarvā̍ṇi bhū̱tāni̱ samī̍kṣantām mi̱trasyā̱haṃ cakṣu̍ṣā sarvā̍ṇi bhū̱tāni̱ samī̍kṣe | mi̱trasya̱ cakṣu̍ṣā samī̍kṣāmahe
300.d: दृ̱ते दृम्̐ह̍ मा मि̱त्रस्य̍ मा̱ चक्षु̍षा सर्वा̍णि भू̱तानि̱ समी̍क्षन्ताम् मि̱त्रस्या̱हं चक्षु̍षा सर्वा̍णि भू̱तानि̱ समी̍क्षे । मि̱त्रस्य̱ चक्षु̍षा समी̍क्षामहे
300.m: O firm one, make me firm. May all beings look upon me with the eye of a friend; / with the eye of a friend I look upon all beings; with the eye of a friend we look [upon each other].

300.s: dṛ̱te dṛm̐ha̍ mā | jyokte̍ sa̱ṃdṛśi̍ jī̱vyāsa̱ṃ jyokte̍ sa̱ṃdṛśi̍ jī̱vyāsam
300.d: दृ̱ते दृम्̐ह̍ मा । ज्योक्ते̍ स̱ंदृशि̍ जी̱व्यास̱ं ज्योक्ते̍ स̱ंदृशि̍ जी̱व्यासम्
300.m: O firm one, make me firm. Long may I live in your sight; long may I live in your sight.

300.s: nama̍ste hara̍se śo̱ciṣe̱ nama̍ste astva̱rciṣe̍ a̱nyām̐ste̍ a̱smatta̍pantu he̱taya̍ḥ pāva̱ko a̱smabhya̍m̐ śi̱vo bha̍va
300.d: नम̍स्ते हर̍से शो̱चिषे̱ नम̍स्ते अस्त्व̱र्चिषे̍ अ̱न्याम्̐स्ते̍ अ̱स्मत्त̍पन्तु हे̱तय̍ः पाव̱को अ̱स्मभ्य̍म्̐ शि̱वो भ̍व
300.m: Homage to your heat and to your flare; homage be to your flame; / let your missiles burn others away from us; as a purifier, be auspicious to us.

300.s: adhyāyaḥ
300.d: अध्यायः

300.s: kāṇva-saṃhitā
300.d: काण्व-संहिता

300.s: nama̍ste astu vi̱dyute̱ nama̍ste stanayi̱tnave̍ nama̍ste bhagavannastu̱ yata̱ḥ sva̱ḥ samī̍hase
300.d: नम̍स्ते अस्तु वि̱द्युते̱ नम̍स्ते स्तनयि̱त्नवे̍ नम̍स्ते भगवन्नस्तु̱ यत̱ः स्व̱ः समी̍हसे
300.m: Homage be to your lightning; homage to your thunder; / homage be to you, O bountiful one, from wherever you strive for heaven.

300.s: yato̍yataḥ sa̱mīha̍se̱ tato̍ no̱ abha̍yaṃ kuru śaṃ na̍ḥ kuru pra̱jābhyo'bha̍yaṃ naḥ pa̱śubhya̍ḥ
300.d: यतो̍यतः स̱मीह̍से̱ ततो̍ नो̱ अभ̍यं कुरु शं न̍ः कुरु प्र̱जाभ्योऽभ̍यं नः प̱शुभ्य̍ः
300.m: From wherever you strive, make us free from fear; / grant peace to our offspring, freedom from fear to our cattle.

300.s: su̱mi̱triyā na̱ āpa̱ oṣa̍dhayaḥ santu durmitri̱yāstasmai̍ santu yo'smāndveṣṭi̱ yaṃ ca̍ va̱yaṃ dvi̱ṣmaḥ
300.d: सु̱मि̱त्रिया न̱ आप̱ ओष̍धयः सन्तु दुर्मित्रि̱यास्तस्मै̍ सन्तु योऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि̱ यं च̍ व̱यं द्वि̱ष्मः
300.m: Friendly to us be the waters and the plants; unfriendly let them be to him / who hates us and whom we hate.

300.s: taccakṣu̍rde̱vahi̍taṃ pu̱rastā̍cchu̱kramuccara̍t paśye̍ma śa̱rada̍ḥ śa̱taṃ jīve̍ma śa̱rada̍ḥ śa̱tam̐ śṛṇu̍yāma śa̱rada̍ḥ śa̱tam
300.d: तच्चक्षु̍र्दे̱वहि̍तं पु̱रस्ता̍च्छु̱क्रमुच्चर̍त् पश्ये̍म श̱रद̍ः श̱तं जीवे̍म श̱रद̍ः श̱तम्̐ शृणु̍याम श̱रद̍ः श̱तम्
300.m: That bright eye established by the gods rising up in the east: / may we see a hundred autumns, may we live a hundred autumns, may we hear a hundred autumns.

300.m: [The section beginning with] 'Verse and speech' has twenty-four [verses] in one anuvāka. / Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter in the Śukla Yajurveda Kāṇva Saṃhitā.

302.s: svāhā̍ ma̱rudbhi̍: pa̱ri̍ śrīyasva di̱vaḥ sa̱m̐spṛśa̍spā̱hi | madhu̱ madhu̱ madhu̍
302.d: स्वाहा̍ म̱रुद्भि̍: प̱रि̍ श्रीयस्व दि̱वः स̱म्̐स्पृश̍स्पा̱हि । मधु̱ मधु̱ मधु̍

303.s: (2) garbho̍ de̱vānā̍ṃ pi̱tā ma̍tī̱nāṃ pati̍: pra̱jānā̍m saṃ de̱vo de̱vena̍ savi̱trā ga̍ta̱ sam̐ sūrye̍ṇa rocate
303.d: (2) गर्भो̍ दे̱वाना̍ं पि̱ता म̍ती̱नां पति̍: प्र̱जाना̍म् सं दे̱वो दे̱वेन̍ सवि̱त्रा ग̍त̱ सम्̐ सूर्ये̍ण रोचते

303.s: sama̱gnira̱gninā̍ gata̱ saṃ daive̍na savi̱trā sam̐ sūrye̍ṇārociṣṭa svāhā̱ sama̱gnistapa̍sā gata̱ saṃ daivye̍na savi̱trā sam̐ sūrye̍ṇārūrucata
303.d: सम̱ग्निर̱ग्निना̍ गत̱ सं दैवे̍न सवि̱त्रा सम्̐ सूर्ये̍णारोचिष्ट स्वाहा̱ सम̱ग्निस्तप̍सा गत̱ सं दैव्ये̍न सवि̱त्रा सम्̐ सूर्ये̍णारूरुचत

303.s: dha̱rtā di̱vo vi bhā̍ti̱ tapa̍saspṛthi̱vyāṃ dha̱rtā de̱vo de̱vānā̱mama̍rtyastapo̱jāḥ vāca̍ma̱sme ni ya̍ccha de̱vāyuva̍m
303.d: ध̱र्ता दि̱वो वि भा̍ति̱ तप̍सस्पृथि̱व्यां ध̱र्ता दे̱वो दे̱वाना̱मम̍र्त्यस्तपो̱जाः वाच̍म̱स्मे नि य̍च्छ दे̱वायुव̍म्

303.s: apa̍śyaṃ go̱pāmani̍padyamāna̱mā ca̱ parā̍ ca pa̱thibhi̱ścara̍ntam sa sa̱dhrīcī̍: sa viṣū̍cī̱rvasā̍na̱ ā va̍rīvarti̱ bhuva̍neṣva̱ntaḥ
303.d: अप̍श्यं गो̱पामनि̍पद्यमान̱मा च̱ परा̍ च प̱थिभि̱श्चर̍न्तम् स स̱ध्रीची̍: स विषू̍ची̱र्वसा̍न̱ आ व̍रीवर्ति̱ भुव̍नेष्व̱न्तः

303.s: viśvā̍sāṃ bhuvāṃ pate̱ viśva̍sya manasaspate̱ viśva̍sya vacasaspate̱ sarva̍sya vacasaspate de̱vaśruttva̍ṃ de̱va gha̱rma de̱vo de̱vānpāhyatra̍ prāvī̱ranu̍ vāṃ de̱vavī̍taye madhu̍ mādhvī̱bhyāṃ madhu̍ mādhū̍cībhyām hṛ̱de tvā̱ mana̍se tvā di̱ve tvā̱ sūryā̍ya tvā | ū̱rdhvo a̍dhva̱raṃ di̱vi de̱veṣu̍ dhehi
303.d: विश्वा̍सां भुवां पते̱ विश्व̍स्य मनसस्पते̱ विश्व̍स्य वचसस्पते̱ सर्व̍स्य वचसस्पते दे̱वश्रुत्त्व̍ं दे̱व घ̱र्म दे̱वो दे̱वान्पाह्यत्र̍ प्रावी̱रनु̍ वां दे̱ववी̍तये मधु̍ माध्वी̱भ्यां मधु̍ माधू̍चीभ्याम् हृ̱दे त्वा̱ मन̍से त्वा दि̱वे त्वा̱ सूर्या̍य त्वा । ऊ̱र्ध्वो अ̍ध्व̱रं दि̱वि दे̱वेषु̍ धेहि

303.s: pi̱tā nau̍'si pi̱tā nau̍ bodhi̱ nama̍ste astu̱ mā mā̍ him̐sīḥ tvaṣṭṛ̍mantastvā sapema pu̱trānpa̱śūnmayi̍ dhehyari̍ṣṭā̱ham̐ sa̱ha patyā̍ bhūyāsam
303.d: पि̱ता नौ̍ऽसि पि̱ता नौ̍ बोधि̱ नम̍स्ते अस्तु̱ मा मा̍ हिम्̐सीः त्वष्टृ̍मन्तस्त्वा सपेम पु̱त्रान्प̱शून्मयि̍ धेह्यरि̍ष्टा̱हम्̐ स̱ह पत्या̍ भूयासम्

303.s: aha̍ḥ ke̱tunā̍ juṣatām̐ su̱jyoti̱rjyoti̍ṣā̱ svāhā̍ rātri̍ḥ ke̱tunā̍ juṣatām̐ su̱jyoti̱rjyoti̍ṣā̱ svāhā̍
303.d: अह̍ः के̱तुना̍ जुषताम्̐ सु̱ज्योति̱र्ज्योति̍षा̱ स्वाहा̍ रात्रि̍ः के̱तुना̍ जुषताम्̐ सु̱ज्योति̱र्ज्योति̍षा̱ स्वाहा̍

303.s:
devasya tvā daśa
yamāya tisraḥ
garbho devānāṃ sapta
'yanuvākeṣu viṃśatiḥ
303.d:
देवस्य त्वा दश
यमाय तिस्रः
गर्भो देवानां सप्त
ऽयनुवाकेषु विंशतिः

304.s: de̱vasya̍ tvā savi̱tuḥ pra̍sa̱ve'śvino̍rbā̱hubhyā̍ṃ pū̱ṣṇo hastā̍bhyām ā da̍de'di̍tyai̱ rāsnā̍si
304.d: दे̱वस्य̍ त्वा सवि̱तुः प्र̍स̱वेऽश्विनो̍र्बा̱हुभ्या̍ं पू̱ष्णो हस्ता̍भ्याम् आ द̍देऽदि̍त्यै̱ रास्ना̍सि
304.m: At the impulse of god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take you: you are a woman.

304.s: adi̍tyai̱ rāsnā̍sīndrā̱ṇyā uṣṇīṣa̍ḥ | pū̱ṣāsi̍ gha̱rmāya̍ dīṣva
304.d: अदि̍त्यै̱ रास्ना̍सीन्द्रा̱ण्या उष्णीष̍ः । पू̱षासि̍ घ̱र्माय̍ दीष्व

304.s: a̱śvibhyā̍ṃ pinvasva̱ sara̍svatyai pinva̱svendrā̍ya pinvasva | svāhendra̍vatsvāhendra̍vatsvāhendra̍vat
yaste̱ stana̍ḥ śaśa̱yo yo ma̍yo̱bhūryo ra̍tna̱dhā va̍su̱vidyaḥ su̱datra̍ḥ yena̱ viśvā̍ pu̱ṣyasi̱ vāryā̍ṇi̱ sara̍svati̱ tami̱ha dhāta̍ve'kaḥ | u̱rva̍ntari̍kṣa̱manve̍mi
304.d: यस्ते̱ स्तन̍ः शश̱यो यो म̍यो̱भूर्यो र̍त्न̱धा व̍सु̱विद्यः सु̱दत्र̍ः येन̱ विश्वा̍ पु̱ष्यसि̱ वार्या̍णि̱ सर̍स्वति̱ तमि̱ह धात̍वेऽकः । उ̱र्व̍न्तरि̍क्ष̱मन्वे̍मि

304.s:
gā̱ya̱traṃ chando̍'si̱ traiṣṭu̍bha̱ṃ chando̍'si̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vībhyā̍ṃ tvā̱ pari̍ gṛhṇāmya̱ntari̍kṣeṇo̱pa ya̍cchāmi indrā̍śvi̱nā madhuna̍ḥ sā̱raghasya̍ gha̱rmaṃ pā̍ta̱ vasa̍vo yaja̍ta̱ vāṭ svāhā̱ sūrya̍sya ra̱śmaye̍ vṛṣṭi̱vana̍ye
(1)
304.d:
गा̱य̱त्रं छन्दो̍ऽसि̱ त्रैष्टु̍भ̱ं छन्दो̍ऽसि̱ द्यावा̍पृथि̱वीभ्या̍ं त्वा̱ परि̍ गृह्णाम्य̱न्तरि̍क्षेणो̱प य̍च्छामि इन्द्रा̍श्वि̱ना मधुन̍ः सा̱रघस्य̍ घ̱र्मं पा̍त̱ वस̍वो यज̍त̱ वाट् स्वाहा̱ सूर्य̍स्य र̱श्मये̍ वृष्टि̱वन̍ये
(1)

305.s: sa̱mu̱drāya̍ tvā̱ vātā̍ya̱ svāhā̍ sali̱rāya̍ tvā̱ vātā̍ya̱ svāhā̍ anā̍dhṛṣyāya tvā̱ vātā̍ya̱ svāhā̍pratidhṛṣyā̱ya tvā̱ vātā̍ya̱ svāhā̍ a̱va̱syave̍ tvā̱ vātā̍ya̱ svāhā̍śimi̱dāga̍ṃ tvā̱ vātā̍ya̱ svāhā̍
305.d: स̱मु̱द्राय̍ त्वा̱ वाता̍य̱ स्वाहा̍ सलि̱राय̍ त्वा̱ वाता̍य̱ स्वाहा̍ अना̍धृष्याय त्वा̱ वाता̍य̱ स्वाहा̍प्रतिधृष्या̱य त्वा̱ वाता̍य̱ स्वाहा̍ अ̱व̱स्यवे̍ त्वा̱ वाता̍य̱ स्वाहा̍शिमि̱दाग̍ं त्वा̱ वाता̍य̱ स्वाहा̍

305.s: indrā̍ya tvā̱ vasu̍mate ru̱drava̍te̱ svāhendrā̍ya tvādi̱tyava̍te̱ svāhā̍ indrā̍ya tvābhimāti̱ghne svāhā̍ savi̱tre tva̍ ṛbhu̱mate̍ vibhu̱mate̱ vāja̍vate̱ svāhā̱ bṛha̱spata̍ye tvā vi̱śvade̍vyāvate̱ svāhā̍
305.d: इन्द्रा̍य त्वा̱ वसु̍मते रु̱द्रव̍ते̱ स्वाहेन्द्रा̍य त्वादि̱त्यव̍ते̱ स्वाहा̍ इन्द्रा̍य त्वाभिमाति̱घ्ने स्वाहा̍ सवि̱त्रे त्व̍ ऋभु̱मते̍ विभु̱मते̱ वाज̍वते̱ स्वाहा̱ बृह̱स्पत̍ये त्वा वि̱श्वदे̍व्यावते̱ स्वाहा̍

305.s: ya̱māya̱ tvāṅgi̍rasvate pitṛ̱mate̱ svāhā̍ | svāhā̍ gha̱rmāya̱ svāhā̍ gha̱rmaḥ pi̱tre
305.d: य̱माय̱ त्वाङ्गि̍रस्वते पितृ̱मते̱ स्वाहा̍ । स्वाहा̍ घ̱र्माय̱ स्वाहा̍ घ̱र्मः पि̱त्रे

305.s: viśvā̱ āśā̍ dakṣi̱ṇasa̍tsavī̱n‌de̱vāna̍yā̱ḷiha svāhā̍kṛtasya gha̱rmasya̱ madho̍: pibatamaśvinā
305.d: विश्वा̱ आशा̍ दक्षि̱णस̍त्सवी̱न्‌दे̱वान̍या̱ऌइह स्वाहा̍कृतस्य घ̱र्मस्य̱ मधो̍: पिबतमश्विना

305.s: di̱vi dhā̍ i̱maṃ ya̱jñami̱maṃ ya̱jñaṃ di̱vi dhā̍: | svāhā̱gnaye̍ ya̱jñiyā̍ya̱ śaṃ yaju̍rbhyaḥ
305.d: दि̱वि धा̍ इ̱मं य̱ज्ञमि̱मं य̱ज्ञं दि̱वि धा̍: । स्वाहा̱ग्नये̍ य̱ज्ञिया̍य̱ शं यजु̍र्भ्यः

305.s: a̱śvinā̍ gha̱rmaṃ pā̍ta̱m̐ hārdā̍na̱maha̍rdivābhi̍rū̱tibhi̍: ta̱ntrāyi̍ṇe̱ namo̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vībhyā̍m
305.d: अ̱श्विना̍ घ̱र्मं पा̍त̱म्̐ हार्दा̍न̱मह̍र्दिवाभि̍रू̱तिभि̍: त̱न्त्रायि̍णे̱ नमो̱ द्यावा̍पृथि̱वीभ्या̍म्

305.s: apā̍tāma̱śvinā̍ gha̱rmamanu̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī ama̍m̐sātām | i̱haiva rā̱taya̍: santu
305.d: अपा̍ताम̱श्विना̍ घ̱र्ममनु̱ द्यावा̍पृथि̱वी अम̍म्̐साताम् । इ̱हैव रा̱तय̍: सन्तु

305.s: i̱ṣe pi̍nvasvo̱rje pi̍nvasva̱ brahma̍ṇe pinvasva kṣa̱trāya̍ pinvasva̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vībhyā̍ṃ pinvasva dha̱rmā̍si sudha̱rmāme̱nya̱sme nṛ̱mṇāni̍ dhāraya̱ brahma̍ dhāraya kṣa̱traṃ dhā̍raya̱ viśa̍ṃ dhāraya
305.d: इ̱षे पि̍न्वस्वो̱र्जे पि̍न्वस्व̱ ब्रह्म̍णे पिन्वस्व क्ष̱त्राय̍ पिन्वस्व̱ द्यावा̍पृथि̱वीभ्या̍ं पिन्वस्व ध̱र्मा̍सि सुध̱र्मामे̱न्य̱स्मे नृ̱म्णानि̍ धारय̱ ब्रह्म̍ धारय क्ष̱त्रं धा̍रय̱ विश̍ं धारय

306.s: svāhā̍ pū̱ṣṇe śa̱rase̱ svāhā̱ grāva̍bhya̱ḥ svāhā̍ prati̱rave̍bhyaḥ svāhā̍ pi̱tṛbhya̍ ū̱rdhvaba̍rhirbhyo gha̱rmapāva̍bhya̱ḥ svāhā̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vībhyā̱m̐ svāhā̱ viśve̍bhyo de̱vebhya̍:
306.d: स्वाहा̍ पू̱ष्णे श̱रसे̱ स्वाहा̱ ग्राव̍भ्य̱ः स्वाहा̍ प्रति̱रवे̍भ्यः स्वाहा̍ पि̱तृभ्य̍ ऊ̱र्ध्वब̍र्हिर्भ्यो घ̱र्मपाव̍भ्य̱ः स्वाहा̱ द्यावा̍पृथि̱वीभ्या̱म्̐ स्वाहा̱ विश्वे̍भ्यो दे̱वेभ्य̍:

306.s: svāhā̍ ru̱drāya̍ rudra̱hūta̍ye̱ svāhā̱ saṃ jyorti̍ṣā̱ jyoti̍: aha̍: ke̱tunā̍ juṣatā̱m̐ sujyo̍ti̱rjyoti̍ṣā̱ svāhā̱ rātri̍: ke̱tunā̍ juṣatā̱m̐ sujyo̍ti̱rjyoti̍ṣā̱ svāhā̍ madhu̍ hu̱tamindra̍tame a̱gnā a̍śyā̱ṃ te de̍va gha̱rma̱ nama̍ste astu̱ mā mā̍ him̐sīḥ
306.d: स्वाहा̍ रु̱द्राय̍ रुद्र̱हूत̍ये̱ स्वाहा̱ सं ज्योर्ति̍षा̱ ज्योति̍: अह̍: के̱तुना̍ जुषता̱म्̐ सुज्यो̍ति̱र्ज्योति̍षा̱ स्वाहा̱ रात्रि̍: के̱तुना̍ जुषता̱म्̐ सुज्यो̍ति̱र्ज्योति̍षा̱ स्वाहा̍ मधु̍ हु̱तमिन्द्र̍तमे अ̱ग्ना अ̍श्या̱ं ते दे̍व घ̱र्म̱ नम̍स्ते अस्तु̱ मा मा̍ हिम्̐सीः
306.m:
Thou art our father; be a father to us; homage be to thee; harm me not.
Accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ may we worship thee; place sons, cattle in me; uninjured may I be with my husband.
